<a id="weather"></a>
## Medium-range weather

### [Accurate medium-range global weather forecasting with 3D neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06185-3)
Bi et al. (2023), *Nature*. 2,087 citations.

- **Main goal:** Achieve medium-range global weather forecasts more accurate than the best operational NWP with AI.
- **Architecture:** Pangu-Weather: 3D Earth-Specific Transformer with Earth-specific positional bias, plus hierarchical temporal aggregation using models at 1, 3, 6 and 24 h steps.
- **Data:** ERA5 at 0.25 degree, 39 years of data (training 1979-2017; testing on 2018).
- **Main result:** Better deterministic scores than ECMWF operational IFS on all tested variables against reanalysis; also better tropical cyclone tracking than ECMWF-HRES when initialized from reanalysis.
- **Open work:** Operational initial conditions, more variables (e.g. precipitation), and ensembles.
- **Issues:** Evaluated against reanalysis and initialized from reanalysis; smooth forecasts; underestimates extreme intensities; no precipitation output.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adi2336)
Lam et al. (2023), *Science*. 2,081 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a machine learning model that beats operational deterministic NWP for global medium-range forecasting at 0.25 degrees.
- **Architecture:** GraphCast: graph neural network encoder-processor-decoder on an icosahedral multimesh, autoregressive with 6 h steps, about 37M parameters.
- **Data:** ERA5 0.25 degrees, 37 pressure levels; trained on 1979-2017 and tested on 2018 against ECMWF HRES (verified against HRES analysis at t=0).
- **Main result:** Outperforms HRES on 90% of 1380 verification targets for 10-day forecasts, produced in under one minute on a single TPU; better tropical cyclone tracks, atmospheric rivers, and extreme temperatures.
- **Open work:** Probabilistic forecasts, reduced blurring at long leads, and operational use with real-time analyses.
- **Issues:** Deterministic MSE training leads to smoothing at long lead times; trained on reanalysis so inherits its biases; underestimates tropical cyclone intensity; relies on NWP-based initial conditions.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [FourCastNet: A Global Data-driven High-resolution Weather Model using Adaptive Fourier Neural Operators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11214)
Pathak et al. (2022), *arXiv*. 1,398 citations.

- **Main goal:** Build a fast, global, high-resolution (0.25 degree) data-driven weather model that forecasts fine-scale variables like surface wind and precipitation.
- **Architecture:** Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator (AFNO) token mixing within a vision-transformer backbone, applied autoregressively with 6-hour steps, plus a separate diagnostic precipitation network.
- **Data:** ERA5 at 0.25 degree, about 20 variables; training 1979-2015, validation 2016-2017, testing 2018 onward.
- **Main result:** Matches ECMWF IFS at short lead times for large-scale variables and beats it for precipitation; produces a week-long forecast in under 2 seconds, enabling ensembles of thousands of members.
- **Open work:** Coupling to more variables and Earth-system components, better probabilistic ensembles and longer lead times.
- **Issues:** Skill falls below IFS at longer lead times for many variables; trained and evaluated on ERA5, inheriting its biases; deterministic training gives smoothed forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Self-organizing maps: applications to synoptic climatology](https://doi.org/10.3354/cr022013)
Hewitson et al. (2002), *Climate Research*. 667 citations.

- **Main goal:** Introduces self-organizing maps as a tool for synoptic climatology, i.e. classifying atmospheric circulation patterns.
- **Architecture:** Self-organizing map (SOM) neural network used for unsupervised classification of synoptic circulation fields.
- **Data:** Gridded circulation fields such as sea level pressure from reanalysis, with example applications to regional climate.
- **Main result:** SOMs give a continuum of synoptic states that captures circulation variability and links to surface climate more flexibly than discrete classifications.
- **Open work:** Use of SOMs for downscaling and for evaluating climate model circulation.
- **Issues:** Results depend on SOM size and training choices; exact datasets and periods are not reported here.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Neural general circulation models for weather and climate](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07744-y)
Kochkov et al. (2023), *Nature*. 627 citations.

- **Main goal:** Combines physics-based dynamics with ML to achieve skillful weather and ensemble forecasts and stable long climate simulations.
- **Architecture:** NeuralGCM: differentiable spectral dynamical core coupled with a neural network that learns physics tendencies, trained end to end over multi-step rollouts; deterministic and stochastic versions.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis at 2.8, 1.4, and 0.7 degree resolutions; evaluated with WeatherBench 2 on 2020; AMIP-style multi-decade runs with prescribed SST.
- **Main result:** Competitive with ML models at 1-10 days and with the ECMWF ensemble at 1-15 days; tracks climate metrics for decades and produces realistic tropical cyclones at 140 km resolution, with large computational savings.
- **Open work:** Coupling to ocean and land models, and improving generalization to climates different from the training period.
- **Issues:** Does not extrapolate to substantially different future climates; trained on reanalysis; some runs become unstable over long integrations.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [FuXi: a cascade machine learning forecasting system for 15-day global weather forecast](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.12873)
Chen et al. (2023), *npj Climate and Atmospheric Science*. 598 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduce error accumulation in ML weather models so that skill at 15-day lead times matches the ECMWF ensemble mean.
- **Architecture:** Cascade of three pretrained U-Transformer (Swin Transformer V2-based) models specialized for 0-5, 5-10 and 10-15 day lead times; ensemble from perturbed initial conditions and model parameters.
- **Data:** ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis, 39 years, 0.25 degree, 6-hourly; evaluated against ERA5 and ECMWF HRES and ensemble forecasts.
- **Main result:** Comparable to the ECMWF ensemble mean over 15 days; extends skillful lead time over HRES from 9.25 to 10.5 days for Z500 and from 10 to 14.5 days for T2M; ensemble spread is promising.
- **Open work:** Better calibrated ensembles, initialization from operational analyses rather than reanalysis, and extension to subseasonal ranges (later FuXi-S2S).
- **Issues:** Smoothing of forecasts at long leads typical of MSE-trained models; trained on reanalysis so inherits its biases; ensemble perturbations are ad hoc rather than flow-dependent.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A k‐nearest‐neighbor simulator for daily precipitation and other weather variables](https://doi.org/10.1029/1999wr900028)
Rajagopalan et al. (1999), *Water Resources Research*. 449 citations.

- **Main goal:** Simulates daily precipitation and other weather variables for impact studies while preserving their joint dependence without parametric assumptions.
- **Architecture:** k-nearest neighbour resampling weather generator conditioned on the previous day's state; nonparametric, not a neural network.
- **Data:** Daily weather records (precipitation, solar radiation, maximum and minimum temperature, dew point, wind speed) at Salt Lake City, Utah.
- **Main result:** The simulator reproduces key statistics and cross-correlations of the observed variables comparably to or better than a parametric generator.
- **Open work:** Multisite extension and conditioning on climate signals.
- **Issues:** Cannot produce values outside the historical record; depends on choice of k and record length.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Challenges and design choices for global weather and climate models based on machine learning](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-11-3999-2018)
Dueben et al. (2018), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 393 citations.

- **Main goal:** Examine whether deep learning models trained on atmospheric data could compete with physics-based global weather and climate models, and what design choices this entails.
- **Architecture:** Discussion paper with a toy neural-network model for global weather prediction on a coarse grid, used to explore design choices (global vs local networks, inputs, time stepping).
- **Data:** Reanalysis data at coarse resolution for a few variables such as Z500 (ERA-Interim, per knowledge of the paper).
- **Main result:** The toy model shows some short-range skill above persistence but is not competitive with operational NWP; key challenges include data volume, conservation, stability and representing the full system.
- **Open work:** Building larger, more complete networks with proper treatment of the sphere and conservation, and hybrid ML-physics systems.
- **Issues:** Very simple toy model at coarse resolution; results are qualitative and predate modern large ML weather models.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Spherical Fourier Neural Operators: Learning Stable Dynamics on the Sphere](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03838)
Bonev et al. (2023), *International Conference on Machine Learning*. 381 citations.

- **Main goal:** Removes the flat-geometry artifacts and dissipation of Fourier neural operators when learning dynamics on the sphere.
- **Architecture:** Spherical Fourier Neural Operator (SFNO), which replaces the discrete Fourier transform with spherical harmonic transforms for rotation-equivariant global convolutions.
- **Data:** Shallow-water equations on the sphere and ERA5 reanalysis for atmospheric forecasting.
- **Main result:** Stable autoregressive rollouts for a year of simulated time (1,460 six-hour steps) with physically plausible dynamics, avoiding the artifacts of standard FNOs.
- **Open work:** Use for long climate simulations and coupled Earth system emulation.
- **Issues:** Stability is shown but long rollouts still smooth small scales; deterministic training; skill comparisons with operational systems are limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Atmospheric Temperature Prediction using Support Vector Machines](https://doi.org/10.7763/ijcte.2009.v1.9)
Radhika et al. (2009), *International Journal of Computer Theory and Engineering*. 367 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts next-day atmospheric (maximum) temperature from past observations as an alternative to conventional statistical forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine regression with a nonlinear kernel, compared against a multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network trained with backpropagation.
- **Data:** Daily temperature records from a single weather station, using the previous few days as inputs.
- **Main result:** The support vector machine gives lower errors than the MLP for one-day-ahead temperature prediction.
- **Open work:** Adding other meteorological predictors, longer lead times and more stations would test generality.
- **Issues:** Single station and short horizon; univariate inputs; no comparison with numerical weather prediction or persistence baselines reported.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [An ensemble of neural networks for weather forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00521-004-0413-4)
Maqsood et al. (2004), *Neural computing & applications (Print)*. 366 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves 24-hour weather forecasting of temperature, wind speed and relative humidity by combining several neural network models.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble of neural networks: multilayer perceptron (MLP), Elman recurrent network, radial basis function network and Hopfield model, combined into an ensemble forecast.
- **Data:** Hourly surface weather observations from southern Saskatchewan (Regina area), Canada, split by season.
- **Main result:** The ensemble of neural networks is more accurate than the individual networks, with the radial basis function network the strongest single model.
- **Open work:** Extending to more variables, longer lead times and other sites, and weighting ensemble members adaptively.
- **Issues:** Single location; point forecasts only, no probabilistic output; no comparison against numerical weather prediction.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [The operational medium-range deterministic weather forecasting can be extended beyond a 10-day lead time](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-025-02502-y)
Chen et al. (2023), *Communications Earth &amp; Environment*. 357 citations.

- **Main goal:** Extends skillful global medium-range deterministic forecasts beyond 10 days and adds probabilistic forecasting.
- **Architecture:** FengWu: transformer-based multi-modal, multi-task model with a replay buffer to reduce error accumulation; FengWu-Ensemble uses a conditional diffusion model on deterministic forecasts.
- **Data:** ERA5 at 0.25 degrees on 13 pressure levels; compared with ECMWF HRES, Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, and the IFS ensemble.
- **Main result:** Outperforms HRES, Pangu-Weather, and GraphCast deterministically, with skillful forecasts beyond 10 days; FengWu-Ensemble beats the IFS ensemble on several variables and metrics.
- **Open work:** Higher resolution, more variables, and operational initialization from real-time analyses.
- **Issues:** Trained and verified against ERA5; deterministic forecasts likely smooth at long leads; ensemble built on deterministic output may limit spread realism.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Improving Data‐Driven Global Weather Prediction Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks on a Cubed Sphere](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020ms002109)
Weyn et al. (2020), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 352 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improve data-driven global weather prediction with CNNs so forecasts are stable and skilful, as a fast tool for large ensembles.
- **Architecture:** Deep U-Net-style CNN operating on a cubed-sphere grid with volume-conservative remapping and face-aware padding, trained with a loss over multiple steps of the prediction sequence.
- **Data:** Reanalysis (ERA5, coarse resolution) for a few basic atmospheric variables, with prescribed top-of-atmosphere solar forcing.
- **Main result:** Indefinitely stable forecasts with realistic patterns at multi-week leads and a realistic seasonal cycle; beats persistence, climatology and a coarse NWP model but is worse than high-resolution operational NWP.
- **Open work:** Adding variables (e.g. precipitation), higher resolution and ensemble generation for sub-seasonal forecasting (pursued in Weyn et al. 2021).
- **Issues:** Limited variable set and coarse resolution; not competitive with operational NWP at medium range; deterministic and smooth.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Searching for analogues, how long must we wait?](https://doi.org/10.3402/tellusa.v46i3.15481)
Dool (1994), *Tellus A*. 342 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates how long an observational record is needed to find good atmospheric analogues for analogue forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Analysis of analogue (nearest-neighbour) forecasting based on the dimensionality of atmospheric states; non-ML statistical method.
- **Data:** Historical atmospheric analyses of Northern Hemisphere circulation fields.
- **Main result:** Finding close analogues for the full hemispheric state would require an impractically long record, on the order of 10^30 years, so analogues are only useful in small domains or few dimensions.
- **Open work:** Constructed analogues and dimension reduction to make analogue methods useful.
- **Issues:** Estimates depend on assumed degrees of freedom and similarity measures.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A study of optimal model lag and spatial inputs to artificial neural network for rainfall forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-1694(99)00165-1)
Luk et al. (2000), *Journal of Hydrology*. 329 citations.

- **Main goal:** Determines optimal input lags and spatial inputs for neural network short-term rainfall forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (MLP) with varying temporal lags and numbers of neighbouring gauges as inputs.
- **Data:** 15-minute rainfall records from a gauge network in the Upper Parramatta River catchment, Sydney, Australia.
- **Main result:** Networks with fewer, well-chosen lags and spatial inputs forecast better than those with many inputs; the optimal lag relates to rainfall autocorrelation.
- **Open work:** Applying the input selection to longer horizons and other catchments.
- **Issues:** Single catchment; very short horizons; rainfall forecasting from gauges alone is limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Can Machines Learn to Predict Weather? Using Deep Learning to Predict Gridded 500‐hPa Geopotential Height From Historical Weather Data](https://doi.org/10.1029/2019ms001705)
Weyn et al. (2019), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 325 citations.

- **Main goal:** Test whether CNNs trained only on historical data can forecast gridded 500-hPa geopotential height without physics.
- **Architecture:** Deep convolutional neural networks (including convolutional LSTM variants) forecasting one or two fields iteratively in time steps.
- **Data:** Climate Forecast System Reanalysis (CFSR) Northern Hemisphere grids (about 2.5 deg), with training on earlier decades and testing on later years.
- **Main result:** Up to 3 days CNNs beat persistence, climatology and barotropic vorticity models but not an operational full-physics model (GFS); adding 700-300 hPa thickness helps; realistic states up to 14 days.
- **Open work:** More variables and levels, global grids, and use of CNN efficiency for large ensembles.
- **Issues:** Coarse resolution and very few variables; well behind operational NWP; trained on reanalysis.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A combined neural-wavelet model for prediction of Ligvanchai watershed precipitation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2008.09.003)
Nourani et al. (2009), *Engineering applications of artificial intelligence*. 321 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts watershed precipitation by capturing multiscale behaviour of rainfall series.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid wavelet-ANN: wavelet decomposition of precipitation series feeding a feed-forward artificial neural network (MLP).
- **Data:** Precipitation records from gauges in the Ligvanchai watershed, Tabriz, Iran.
- **Main result:** The wavelet-ANN model forecasts precipitation better than an ANN without wavelet preprocessing, for both short- and long-term behaviour.
- **Open work:** Choice of wavelet and decomposition levels and adding climate predictors.
- **Issues:** Single small watershed; wavelet preprocessing may introduce boundary effects or information leakage if applied non-causally.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [An application of artificial neural networks for rainfall forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0895-7177(00)00272-7)
Luk et al. (2001), *Mathematical and Computer Modelling*. 319 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops neural network models for short-term rainfall forecasting in an urban catchment.
- **Architecture:** Compares three artificial neural network types: multilayer feed-forward network (MLP), Elman partial recurrent network and time-delay neural network.
- **Data:** 15-minute rainfall data from a gauge network in the Upper Parramatta River catchment, Sydney, Australia.
- **Main result:** All three network types give similar, reasonable forecasts; networks with fewer inputs perform comparably with more complex ones.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and use of radar or meteorological inputs.
- **Issues:** Very short lead times; gauge-only inputs; single catchment.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Forecasting Global Weather with Graph Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.07575)
Keisler (2022), *arXiv*. 305 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develop a data-driven global weather forecasting model that steps the full 3D atmospheric state forward and is competitive with operational NWP.
- **Architecture:** Graph neural network with an encoder-processor-decoder design mapping the lat-lon grid to an icosahedral mesh; a 6-hour step applied autoregressively over several days.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis or GFS forecast data at 1 degree with a small set of variables on multiple pressure levels; also tested with live operational GFS initial conditions.
- **Main result:** Improves on previous data-driven models for Z500 and T850 and is comparable to operational GFS and ECMWF forecasts when evaluated at 1-degree scales with reanalysis initial conditions.
- **Open work:** Higher resolution, more variables and levels, and better performance from operational (rather than reanalysis) initial conditions.
- **Issues:** Coarse 1-degree evaluation; comparison favours the model when initialized from reanalysis; forecasts smooth with lead time and are deterministic only.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Artificial neural network technique for rainfall forecasting applied to the São Paulo region](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2004.06.028)
Ramírez et al. (2005), *Journal of Hydrology*. 299 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves quantitative rainfall forecasts over the São Paulo region by post-processing numerical model output.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward artificial neural network (MLP) used for statistical downscaling of Eta regional model output, compared with multiple linear regression.
- **Data:** Eta model forecast fields and rain gauge observations over the São Paulo region, Brazil.
- **Main result:** The neural network rainfall forecasts outperform multiple linear regression and the raw Eta model.
- **Open work:** Applying to other seasons and regions and to probabilistic forecasts.
- **Issues:** Dependent on Eta model biases; limited validation period; heavy rainfall events are few.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [AIFS -- ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01465)
Lang et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 297 citations.

- **Main goal:** Describes ECMWF's operational data-driven global medium-range forecasting system.
- **Architecture:** AIFS: graph neural network encoder and decoder with a sliding-window transformer processor; modular design with several levels of parallelism.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis and ECMWF operational NWP analyses; verified against analyses and observations.
- **Main result:** Highly skilled forecasts for upper-air variables, surface weather parameters, and tropical cyclone tracks; runs four times daily with open data.
- **Open work:** Probabilistic versions, higher resolution, and more variables.
- **Issues:** Deterministic version tends to smooth; depends on NWP analyses for initialization; much verification is against ECMWF's own analysis.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A Deep Hybrid Model for Weather Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1145/2783258.2783275)
Grover et al. (2015), *Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining*. 284 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves short-range weather forecasts of surface variables at station locations by learning from historical observations rather than running a full numerical weather prediction model.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid model combining discriminatively trained per-station predictors with a deep generative component that models joint spatial statistics across stations; the exact network family is not specified here.
- **Data:** Historical surface weather station observations over the United States (e.g., temperature, pressure, wind); exact network and period not given here.
- **Main result:** The hybrid model improves forecasts over purely discriminative baselines and is reported to be competitive with operational forecasts at short leads.
- **Open work:** Adding more variables, longer lead times and integration with NWP output.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; architecture details and benchmark comparisons rely on recollection and should be checked; station-only data.

### [Toward Data‐Driven Weather and Climate Forecasting: Approximating a Simple General Circulation Model With Deep Learning](https://doi.org/10.1029/2018gl080704)
Scher (2018), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 265 citations.

- **Main goal:** Test whether a deep neural network can emulate the full dynamics of a simple general circulation model for both weather-like forecasts and climate runs.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional encoder-decoder style neural network predicting the full model state ahead, iterated autoregressively for long runs.
- **Data:** Long simulation output from a simplified GCM (PUMA, dry dynamics without seasonal cycle) used for training and testing.
- **Main result:** The network predicts the model state several time steps ahead and, iterated from arbitrary states, produces a stable climate run with similar statistics and no long-term drift, without built-in conservation.
- **Open work:** Move to more complex models (moisture, seasonal cycle) and eventually real atmospheric data; study of the sources of stability.
- **Issues:** Simple, idealized model world with no seasonal cycle; forecast skill degrades quickly; results may not transfer to realistic atmospheres.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Data‐Driven Medium‐Range Weather Prediction With a Resnet Pretrained on Climate Simulations: A New Model for WeatherBench](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020ms002405)
Rasp et al. (2020), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 244 citations.

- **Main goal:** Advance purely data-driven medium-range weather prediction and set a stronger WeatherBench baseline.
- **Architecture:** Deep residual convolutional neural network (ResNet) predicting directly at each lead time, pretrained on climate model output and fine-tuned on reanalysis.
- **Data:** WeatherBench ERA5 at 5.625°, with pretraining on CMIP6 historical simulations; geopotential, temperature and precipitation up to 5 days.
- **Main result:** Outperforms earlier WeatherBench submissions and is comparable to a physical model run at similar coarse resolution (e.g. Z500 RMSE around 268 m2/s2 at 3 days and about 500 at 5 days); learned correlations look physically reasonable.
- **Open work:** Scaling experiments suggest higher resolution and more data could improve skill further.
- **Issues:** Coarse 5.625° resolution; far behind operational IFS; deterministic forecasts blur at longer leads.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Interpretable weather forecasting for worldwide stations with a unified deep model](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-023-00667-9)
Wu et al. (2023), *Nature Machine Intelligence*. 240 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts weather at thousands of worldwide stations with one unified deep model that captures spatiotemporal correlations among stations and remains interpretable.
- **Architecture:** Corrformer, a transformer with a multi-correlation mechanism that replaces standard attention to model spatial and temporal correlations efficiently.
- **Data:** Global station observations (temperature and wind) from several thousand weather stations (NCEI global surface data); exact counts not verified here.
- **Main result:** Corrformer outperforms state-of-the-art deep forecasting models and is reported to be competitive with operational numerical forecasts at the station level, with interpretable correlations.
- **Open work:** Adding more variables, longer leads and coupling with gridded NWP or reanalysis data.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; station-only data, limited variables; numbers not verified here.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Rainfall forecasting by technological machine learning models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.amc.2007.10.046)
Hong (2008), *Applied Mathematics and Computation*. 240 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts rainfall using machine learning models.
- **Architecture:** Recurrent support vector regression with chaotic particle swarm optimization for parameter selection.
- **Data:** Rainfall records from Taiwan; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The proposed model forecasts rainfall more accurately than the comparison models.
- **Open work:** Testing at more sites and lead times.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; data and error figures are not reported here.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [End-to-end data-driven weather prediction](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08897-0)
Allen et al. (2025), *Nature*. 206 citations.

- **Main goal:** Replaces the entire NWP pipeline (data assimilation, forecasting, post-processing) with a single end-to-end ML system.
- **Architecture:** Aardvark Weather: an encoder that maps raw observations to a gridded state, a processor for forecasting, and decoders for local station forecasts, fine-tuned end to end.
- **Data:** Raw satellite, in situ and station observations as inputs; ERA5 as gridded training target (about 1.5° resolution).
- **Main result:** Global forecasts beat an operational NWP baseline for some variables and lead times; station forecasts are skillful to 10 days, competing with post-processed NWP.
- **Open work:** Higher resolution, more observations and variables, and customized models for end users.
- **Issues:** Coarse resolution; trained against ERA5 so still depends on NWP-derived targets; does not beat the best operational systems overall.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Optimized scenario for rainfall forecasting using genetic algorithm coupled with artificial neural network](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2007.08.033)
Nasseri et al. (2008), *Expert systems with applications*. 194 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts rainfall with an optimized neural network whose structure and inputs are selected by a genetic algorithm.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network (MLP) coupled with a genetic algorithm for optimizing network inputs, structure and weights.
- **Data:** Rainfall gauge records from a catchment in Sydney, Australia; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The genetic-algorithm-optimized network improves rainfall forecasts relative to a conventional neural network.
- **Open work:** Test longer lead times and other climates.
- **Issues:** Single catchment; rainfall intermittency limits skill; no probabilistic output.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Precipitation Forecasting Using a Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0434(1999)014<0338:pfuann>2.0.co;2)
Hall et al. (1999), *Weather and Forecasting*. 191 citations.

- **Main goal:** Uses a neural network to forecast precipitation, an early application of machine learning to operational precipitation forecasting.

- **Data:** Not reported in the available metadata (abstract missing).
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Extension to other locations and comparison with operational statistical guidance.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; likely limited to a small region and short training record typical of the period.

### [Improving Snowfall Forecasting by Diagnosing Snow Density](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0434(2003)018<0264:isfbds>2.0.co;2)
Roebber et al. (2003), *Weather and Forecasting*. 191 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves snowfall forecasts by diagnosing snow density (snow ratio) instead of using a fixed 10:1 ratio.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble of artificial neural networks classifying snow ratio into heavy, average and light classes from temperature and humidity profile predictors.
- **Data:** US cooperative observer snowfall and liquid equivalent records matched with radiosonde-derived atmospheric profiles over several decades.
- **Main result:** The neural network ensemble diagnoses snow ratio class substantially better than climatology or the 10:1 rule.
- **Open work:** Apply operationally to model forecast profiles and refine for regional variations.
- **Issues:** Snow measurement errors are large; performance depends on forecast profile accuracy.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Scaling transformer neural networks for skillful and reliable medium-range weather forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03876)
Nguyen et al. (2023), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 171 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identify what makes data-driven medium-range weather models work by building a simple, scalable transformer with careful ablations.
- **Architecture:** Stormer: standard vision-transformer backbone with weather-specific variable embedding, randomized dynamics forecasting over varying intervals, and pressure-weighted loss; multiple interval combinations averaged at inference.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis via WeatherBench 2 (coarse resolution relative to 0.25 degree models).
- **Main result:** Competitive at short-to-medium range and better than existing methods beyond 7 days on WeatherBench 2, with orders of magnitude less training data and compute; accuracy scales with model size and tokens.
- **Open work:** Higher resolution training, probabilistic forecasting and further scaling.
- **Issues:** Lower resolution than leading ML models; deterministic; ensemble-of-intervals mean may smooth forecasts; evaluated against reanalysis.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Predicting clustered weather patterns: A test case for applications of convolutional neural networks to spatio-temporal climate data](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-020-57897-9)
Chattopadhyay et al. (2018), *Scientific Reports*. 161 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests convolutional neural networks for identifying and predicting large-scale weather regimes, using unsupervised clustering to avoid costly human labelling.
- **Architecture:** Deep convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on labels from K-means-style unsupervised clustering, compared with logistic regression.
- **Data:** Daily large-scale circulation patterns over North America from a fully coupled climate model (CESM Large Ensemble), clustered into 4 regimes.
- **Main result:** With at least 1000 samples per cluster accuracy exceeds 90%; with 3000 samples it reaches 94% for identification and 93–76% for 1–5 day prediction, about 25% better than logistic regression.
- **Open work:** Applying the auto-labelling approach to reanalysis and observations, and to other spatio-temporal climate patterns and extremes.
- **Issues:** Trained on climate model output; only 4 coarse regimes; labels inherit clustering choices; prediction skill degrades with lead time.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [On Some Limitations of Current Machine Learning Weather Prediction Models](https://doi.org/10.1029/2023gl107377)
Bonavita (2024), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 152 citations.

- **Main goal:** Examines the fidelity and physical consistency of leading ML weather models beyond headline skill scores.
- **Architecture:** Diagnostic analysis (not a new ML model) of forecasts from Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet and GraphCast, e.g. spectra, balance relationships and small-scale structure.
- **Data:** ML model forecasts initialized from ERA5/operational analyses, compared with ECMWF IFS forecasts and analyses.
- **Main result:** The ML models fail to reproduce sub-synoptic and mesoscale phenomena and lack the fidelity and physical consistency of physics-based models, affecting interpretation of their skill.
- **Open work:** Designing ML models that balance forecast skill with physical realism, and evaluation metrics that reward realism.
- **Issues:** Evaluates early-generation deterministic models trained with MSE losses; newer probabilistic and generative models may address some issues.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Simulation of the Urban Heat Island Phenomenon in Mediterranean Climates](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00024-003-2447-4)
Mihalakakou et al. (2004), *pure and applied geophysics*. 152 citations.

- **Main goal:** Simulates urban heat island intensity in a Mediterranean city to understand and predict urban warming.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network relating urban heat island intensity to meteorological parameters.
- **Data:** Air temperature measurements from urban and suburban stations in Athens, Greece, with meteorological data.

- **Open work:** Extension to other cities and to spatial mapping of the heat island.
- **Issues:** Single-city; statistical model without physical urban processes.

### [Forecast of daily mean, maximum and minimum temperature time series by three artificial neural network methods](https://doi.org/10.1002/met.83)
Ustaoğlu et al. (2008), *Meteorological Applications*. 151 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts daily mean, maximum and minimum air temperature time series.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward backpropagation, radial basis function and generalized regression neural networks compared with each other and with a regression model.
- **Data:** Daily temperature records from stations in Turkey.
- **Main result:** All three neural network types give satisfactory forecasts, with small differences in error among them.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and use of additional meteorological inputs.
- **Issues:** Univariate-type inputs; few stations; no comparison with numerical weather prediction.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Weather and climate forecasting with neural networks: using general circulation models (GCMs) with different complexity as a study ground](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-12-2797-2019)
Scher et al. (2019), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 148 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assess from the bottom up whether neural networks can, in principle, forecast weather and produce climate datasets, using GCMs of varying complexity as simplified reality.
- **Architecture:** Deep convolutional neural networks trained to predict model weather days ahead, run iteratively to test climate reproduction.
- **Data:** Output of the simple GCMs PUMA and PLASIM at different complexity levels and training-period lengths.
- **Main result:** Forecast skill depends on model complexity and training length; reproducing the GCM climate including a seasonal cycle remains challenging, unlike earlier results without seasonal cycle.
- **Open work:** More complex models, longer training data and architectures that maintain stable climates with seasonal cycles.
- **Issues:** Idealized, coarse GCM output rather than reality; limited variables and resolution.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Daily means ambient temperature prediction using artificial neural network method: A case study of Turkey](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.renene.2008.07.007)
Dombaycı et al. (2009), *Renewable Energy*. 141 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts daily mean ambient temperature for energy and engineering applications.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward artificial neural network (MLP) trained with backpropagation-type algorithms.
- **Data:** Daily mean temperature records from a meteorological station in Denizli, Turkey, over a few years.
- **Main result:** The ANN predicts daily mean temperature with low error; exact metrics are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Using more stations and meteorological predictors.
- **Issues:** Single station and short record; inputs largely calendar and lagged temperature.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Machine Learning‐Based Global Atmospheric Forecast Model](https://doi.org/10.1029/2020gl087776)
Arcomano et al. (2020), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 139 citations.

- **Main result:** Hourly 20-day forecasts stay realistic; the model beats climatology and persistence for the first three days in the midlatitudes but not the tropics, and does best versus SPEEDY for variables dominated by parameterized processes.

### [Deep Learning for Day Forecasts from Sparse Observations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.06079)
Andrychowicz et al. (2023), *arXiv*. 134 citations.

Verma et al. (2024), *International Conference on Learning Representations*. 129 citations.

- **Architecture:** Self-organizing map (SOM) clustering of synoptic atmospheric fields.
- **Data:** Reanalysis atmospheric fields and rainfall observations in Japan (Kyushu) during the Baiu season.
- **Main result:** The SOM identifies typical patterns associated with heavy rainfall, linked to moisture flux.
- **Open work:** Use the patterns for heavy rainfall forecasting from model output.
- **Issues:** Pattern identification is descriptive; sensitivity to SOM size.
- *Basis: assessment*

### California Center for Population Research On-line Working Paper Series Weather Regime Prediction Using Statistical Learning Weather Regime Prediction Using Statistical Learning
Deloncle et al. (2005), *Venue not recorded*. 94 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts the persistence and transitions of large-scale atmospheric weather regimes, testing whether statistical learning can extend regime predictability.
- **Architecture:** Statistical learning classifiers, including random forests and nearest-neighbour (analogue) methods, applied to regime prediction.
- **Data:** Long simulations of a quasi-geostrophic atmospheric model with identified weather regimes; observational validation details are not reported here.
- **Main result:** Statistical learning gives some skill in predicting regime breaks and transitions beyond climatology; quantitative scores are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Applying the approach to reanalysis data and operational models and identifying physical precursors of regime transitions.
- **Issues:** Working-paper version; skill mainly demonstrated in an idealized model, so transfer to the real atmosphere is uncertain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### Bayesian Networks for Probabilistic Weather Prediction
Cofiño et al. (2002), *European Conference on Artificial Intelligence*. 88 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides probabilistic local weather (precipitation) forecasts that capture spatial dependencies among stations.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian networks learned from data, encoding dependencies among station variables and atmospheric predictors, with probabilistic inference.
- **Data:** Daily precipitation records from a network of stations in Spain with large-scale atmospheric predictors; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Bayesian networks produce skilful probabilistic forecasts and consistent spatial patterns; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Larger networks, more variables and operational use with NWP outputs.
- **Issues:** Learning structure is costly; discretization of variables loses information.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Weather analogue: A tool for real-time prediction of daily weather data realizations based on a modified k-nearest neighbor approach](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2007.09.011)
Bannayan et al. (2008), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 87 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides real-time realizations of daily weather for the remainder of a season so crop models can forecast yields during the growing season.
- **Architecture:** Weather analogue tool based on a modified k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) resampling approach that selects historical years similar to current conditions; non-parametric nonneural method.
- **Data:** Historical daily weather station records (e.g. temperature, rainfall, solar radiation); stations and periods are not reported here (no abstract available).
- **Main result:** Not reported; no abstract is available for this paper.
- **Open work:** Conditioning the analogue selection on seasonal climate forecasts and evaluating crop-yield forecast skill.
- **Issues:** Analogue resampling cannot produce conditions outside the historical record; card based on title and general knowledge.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Can Artificial Intelligence‐Based Weather Prediction Models Simulate the Butterfly Effect?](https://doi.org/10.1029/2023gl105747)
Selz et al. (2023), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 86 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether AI weather models reproduce the rapid growth of small initial-condition errors (butterfly effect) that limits predictability.
- **Architecture:** Perturbation experiments with an AI-based weather model (Pangu-Weather) compared with physics-based numerical model simulations; not a new ML method.
- **Data:** Initial conditions from ECMWF analyses, with small- and analysis-uncertainty-size perturbations.
- **Main result:** The AI model fails to reproduce rapid initial growth of small perturbations, implying unlimited predictability; for realistic-size perturbations it largely agrees with physical models, with some deficits.
- **Open work:** Training or designing AI models that capture small-scale error growth, and caution in using them for predictability studies.
- **Issues:** Single AI model and limited case set; coarse 0.25° resolution may itself suppress small-scale growth.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [SwinRDM: Integrate SwinRNN with Diffusion Model towards High-Resolution and High-Quality Weather Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.48448/zn7f-fc64)
Chen et al. (2023), *AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence*. 84 citations.

- **Main goal:** Achieve high-resolution, high-quality data-driven medium-range weather forecasts that compete with operational NWP.
- **Architecture:** SwinRDM: an improved SwinRNN (Swin transformer-based recurrent network) forecasting at 1.40625° combined with a diffusion model for super-resolution to 0.25°.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis; evaluated against IFS on Z500, T850, T2M and total precipitation.
- **Main result:** Outperforms IFS on Z500, T850, T2M and TP at lead times up to 5 days at 0.25° resolution.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times, probabilistic forecasting and operational deployment.
- **Issues:** Trained on reanalysis and inherits its biases; evaluated only to 5 days, with the two-step approach possibly adding inconsistencies.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Ceiling and Visibility Forecasts via Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf994.1)
Marzban et al. (2007), *Weather and Forecasting*. 79 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves forecasts of ceiling and visibility, important for aviation, by statistically post-processing numerical model output.
- **Architecture:** Neural networks (multilayer perceptrons) that post-process mesoscale model output and observations to forecast ceiling and visibility.
- **Data:** Numerical model output (MM5) and surface observations at numerous stations in the US Pacific Northwest.
- **Main result:** The neural networks outperform the raw model forecasts of ceiling and visibility at most stations and lead times.
- **Open work:** Probabilistic forecasts and extension to other regions and models.
- **Issues:** Station-specific models and limited samples of low-ceiling and low-visibility events.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### Rainfall Prediction Using Artificial Neural Networks
Lee (1998), *Venue not recorded*. 77 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts rainfall amounts at unsampled locations from a subset of gauge observations, as part of a spatial interpolation comparison.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks, using radial basis function networks for part of the domain and linear regression elsewhere.
- **Data:** Daily rainfall from a Swiss gauge network (Spatial Interpolation Comparison 97 data), with a subset of stations used for training.
- **Main result:** The neural network approach gives reasonable rainfall estimates at unsampled stations; quantitative results are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Inclusion of elevation and other covariates and comparison with geostatistical methods are natural next steps.
- **Issues:** Few training stations and a single day's field; spatial interpolation, not temporal forecasting.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Dewpoint Temperature Prediction Using Artificial Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/2007jamc1693.1)
Shank et al. (2008), *Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology*. 77 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts dewpoint temperature hours ahead to support frost protection and agricultural decisions.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks (feedforward, Ward-style networks) using recent weather observations as inputs for 1–12 h ahead prediction.
- **Data:** Weather data from the Georgia Automated Environmental Monitoring Network (AEMN), USA.
- **Main result:** The neural networks predict dewpoint with errors that grow with lead time and remain useful up to about 12 h ahead.
- **Open work:** Integration into decision-support systems and inclusion of forecast meteorology.
- **Issues:** Station data from one state; errors grow at longer lead times.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A recurrent support vector regression model in rainfall forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1002/hyp.6323)
Pai et al. (2007), *Hydrological Processes*. 77 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts rainfall with a recurrent support vector regression model to capture temporal dependence.
- **Architecture:** Recurrent support vector regression (SVR) model; the abstract and parameter-selection procedure are not available.
- **Data:** Rainfall records; region and period are not reported here (no abstract available).
- **Main result:** Not reported; no abstract is available for this paper.
- **Open work:** Comparison with other machine-learning and stochastic rainfall forecasting models over more sites.
- **Issues:** Card based on the title only.
- *Basis: assessment*

### A fuzzy case-based system for weather prediction
Riordan et al. (2002), *International journal of engineering intelligent systems for electrical engineering and communications*. 75 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts airport weather, notably cloud ceiling and visibility, by retrieving similar past cases from long observation archives.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy case-based reasoning system using fuzzy similarity measures to find nearest neighbour analogue cases and combine their outcomes into a forecast.
- **Data:** Long archives of hourly airport surface observations (Canada); exact stations and period not reported here.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy case-based approach produces ceiling and visibility forecasts more skilful than persistence and competitive with standard references.
- **Open work:** Adding more predictors, more airports and integration into operational forecasting.
- **Issues:** Analogue methods depend on archive size and struggle with rare events; few sites evaluated.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Dynamical Tests of a Deep-Learning Weather Prediction Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.10867)
Hakim et al. (2023), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 70 citations.

- **Main goal:** Test whether a deep-learning weather model (Pangu-Weather) encodes atmospheric dynamics or merely pattern-matches, to judge its use for basic science.
- **Architecture:** No new model; Pangu-Weather is subjected to four classical dynamical experiments using localized perturbations added to steady time-averaged states.
- **Data:** Time-averaged (e.g. winter-mean) background states derived from the reanalysis-based climate on which Pangu-Weather operates; perturbation experiments are idealized.
- **Main result:** Reproduces a Matsuno-Gill response to tropical heating, realistic extratropical cyclones and fronts, geostrophic adjustment in about 6 h, and hurricane genesis above about 4 hPa initial amplitude that vanishes with zero humidity.
- **Open work:** Using such models as fast tools for testing a wide range of dynamical hypotheses, and testing other ML models similarly.
- **Issues:** Qualitative assessment for one model; perturbation responses may partly reflect training-data analogues; no conservation or balance diagnostics beyond the experiments shown.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [SOFM-MLP: a hybrid neural network for atmospheric temperature prediction](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2003.817225)
Pal et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 70 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts daily maximum and minimum atmospheric temperature, motivated by the nonstationary, regime-dependent nature of weather data.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid SOFM-MLP: a self-organizing feature map partitions the input space and a separate multilayer perceptron (MLP) is trained per cluster; a feature-selecting MLP identifies useful inputs.
- **Data:** Daily surface meteorological observations (temperature, pressure, humidity, rainfall, etc.) from a station in India.
- **Main result:** The hybrid SOFM-MLP gives better temperature forecasts than a single MLP, and feature selection reduces inputs without loss of accuracy.
- **Open work:** Extension to other variables, longer leads and multiple stations.
- **Issues:** Single-station data; next-day horizon only; no probabilistic output.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Application of soft computing models to hourly weather analysis in southern Saskatchewan, Canada](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.engappai.2004.08.019)
Maqsood et al. (2005), *Engineering applications of artificial intelligence*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Applies soft computing models to hourly weather analysis and forecasting of surface variables in southern Saskatchewan.
- **Architecture:** Several neural networks, including multilayer perceptron (MLP), Elman recurrent network, radial basis function network and Hopfield model, plus ensembles.
- **Data:** Hourly temperature, wind speed and relative humidity observations from a southern Saskatchewan station (Regina).
- **Main result:** The radial basis function network gives the most accurate hourly forecasts, and ensembles improve on individual networks.
- **Open work:** Longer horizons and more stations.
- **Issues:** Single station; short training period; seasonal stratification limits generality.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [An improved naive Bayesian classifier technique coupled with a novel input solution method [rainfall prediction]](https://doi.org/10.1109/5326.941848)
Liu et al. (2001), *IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man & Cybernetics. Systems*. 69 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves rainfall prediction by addressing weaknesses of naive Bayesian classifiers with correlated and numerous meteorological inputs.
- **Architecture:** Improved naive Bayesian classifier coupled with a new input selection/solution method (genetic-algorithm-based selection of inputs).
- **Data:** Daily meteorological observations used to classify rainfall occurrence; source details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The improved classifier gives higher rainfall prediction accuracy than the standard naive Bayes classifier and compares favourably with other classifiers.
- **Open work:** Testing on other locations and on rainfall amount classes.
- **Issues:** Abstract not available; specifics of data and accuracy are uncertain; independence assumptions remain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Advancing Parsimonious Deep Learning Weather Prediction Using the HEALPix Mesh](https://doi.org/10.1029/2023ms004021)
Karlbauer et al. (2023), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 64 citations.

- **Main goal:** Build a parsimonious deep-learning weather model that stays stable for very long autoregressive rollouts at modest cost.
- **Architecture:** DLWP-HPX: U-Net on the HEALPix mesh with inverted channel depth and gated recurrent units at each U-Net level; location-invariant convolutions.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis, seven prognostic variables, 3-hourly, on a roughly 110 km HEALPix mesh.
- **Main result:** At 1-week lead, skill is about one day behind Pangu-Weather, GraphCast and ECMWF HRES; no loss of spectral power after day 2; realistic 1-year rollouts with seasonal cycle.
- **Open work:** Adding more variables, higher resolution and ocean coupling for subseasonal and climate applications.
- **Issues:** Coarser resolution and fewer variables than state-of-the-art models; deterministic; trained on reanalysis so inherits its biases.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Fuzzy Logic-Based Analog Forecasting System for Ceiling and Visibility](https://doi.org/10.1175/2007waf2006017.1)
Hansen (2007), *Weather and Forecasting*. 63 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts airport ceiling and visibility, which are critical for aviation and hard to predict with NWP, using an analog approach.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic-based analog forecasting: a fuzzy k-nearest neighbour method that finds similar past weather cases using fuzzy similarity measures on observed predictors.
- **Data:** Long archives of hourly airport surface observations (METAR-type) at Canadian airports.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy analog system produces short-term ceiling and visibility forecasts more accurate than persistence and competitive with operational terminal forecasts.
- **Open work:** Incorporating NWP predictors and extending to more airports and longer lead times.
- **Issues:** Skill decays with lead time; depends on archive length; rare low-ceiling events limit analog availability.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Comparative study among different neural net learning algorithms applied to rainfall time series](https://doi.org/10.1002/met.71)
Chattopadhyay et al. (2008), *Meteorological Applications*. 60 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares neural network learning algorithms for predicting rainfall time series.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward neural networks (MLP) trained with different learning algorithms (gradient-descent back-propagation variants, conjugate gradient, Levenberg-Marquardt type).
- **Data:** Indian monsoon rainfall time series; period not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Learning algorithms are compared for rainfall prediction skill; the best algorithm and scores are not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Testing on more rainfall series and predictors.
- **Issues:** Short annual series limit training; univariate inputs only.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A data-to-forecast machine learning system for global weather](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62024-1)
Sun et al. (2024), *Nature Communications*. 59 citations.

- **Main goal:** Remove the dependence of ML weather models on NWP-produced initial conditions by building an end-to-end ML data assimilation and forecasting system.
- **Architecture:** FuXi Weather: ML forecast model coupled with ML-based assimilation of multi-satellite observations in a cycling DA-forecast system.
- **Data:** Multi-satellite observations (fewer than used by conventional NWP); ERA5-type reanalysis for training; compared with ECMWF HRES.
- **Main result:** Reliable 10-day forecasts at 0.25 degree; outperforms ECMWF HRES beyond day one in observation-sparse regions such as central Africa; background forecasts help constrain analysis.
- **Open work:** Adding more observation types (e.g. conventional and in situ data) and probabilistic DA and forecasting.
- **Issues:** Uses fewer observations than operational systems, so global skill may lag HRES in data-rich regions; reliance on reanalysis for training.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Regional data-driven weather modeling with a global stretched-grid](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.02891)
Nipen et al. (2024), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 58 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develop a data-driven model for high-resolution regional forecasting while keeping a global domain for boundary information.
- **Architecture:** Bris: graph neural network built on the AIFS framework with a stretched grid giving high resolution over the Nordics and coarse resolution elsewhere.
- **Data:** Pretrained on 43 years of global ERA5 at 31 km; fine-tuned on 3.3 years of 2.5 km MEPS operational analyses; verified against Norwegian station observations.
- **Main result:** 2.5 km, 6-hourly forecasts; lower 2 m temperature RMSE than both MEPS control and ensemble mean; competitive precipitation and wind speed.
- **Open work:** Improving extremes, increasing temporal resolution and adding probabilistic forecasts.
- **Issues:** Underestimates extreme events; 6-hour time step coarse for short-range needs; short high-resolution training record.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Fixing the Double Penalty in Data-Driven Weather Forecasting Through a Modified Spherical Harmonic Loss Function](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19374)
Subich et al. (2025), *International Conference on Machine Learning*. 57 citations.

- **Main goal:** Removes the fine-scale smoothing that MSE training causes in data-driven weather models through the double-penalty effect.
- **Architecture:** Parameter-free modified spherical harmonic loss that separates decorrelation error from spectral amplitude error, used to fine-tune GraphCast, a graph neural network.
- **Data:** GraphCast fine-tuned on ERA5 reanalysis; evaluated on global medium-range forecasts including tropical cyclones and surface wind extremes.
- **Main result:** Produces sharp deterministic forecasts, raising effective resolution from 1,250 km to 160 km, improving ensemble spread and tropical cyclone strength and surface wind extreme predictions.
- **Open work:** Applying the loss to other architectures and to training from scratch, and assessing its effect on probabilistic and longer-range forecasts.
- **Issues:** Sharper fields may raise RMSE relative to MSE-trained models; demonstrated mainly through fine-tuning a single model.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Modeling ambient air temperature time series using neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1029/98jd02002)
Mihalakakou et al. (1998), *Journal of Geophysical Research*. 57 citations.

- **Main goal:** Models and forecasts ambient air temperature time series, useful for building energy and climate applications.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (multilayer perceptron) trained on past temperature values for time-series prediction.
- **Data:** Hourly or daily air temperature records from Athens, Greece; periods not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** The neural networks reproduce and predict air temperature with good accuracy; exact error statistics not reported here.
- **Open work:** Multi-station testing and inclusion of other meteorological predictors.
- **Issues:** Single-site data; autoregressive network may not handle unusual conditions or long horizons.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Kilometer-scale convection-allowing model emulation using generative diffusion modeling](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adv0423)
Pathak et al. (2024), *Science Advances*. 56 citations.

- **Main goal:** Shows that machine learning can emulate a km-scale convection-allowing model, a regime where deterministic DL had struggled.
- **Architecture:** StormCast: a generative diffusion model that autoregressively predicts 99 state variables with a 1-hour step, conditioned on 26 synoptic-scale variables.
- **Data:** HRRR 3-km operational model output over a central US domain, with coarse ERA5 fields as synoptic conditioning.
- **Main result:** Competitive 1-6 hour forecast skill for composite radar reflectivity and physically realistic convective clusters, moist updrafts and cold pools.
- **Open work:** Improving regional km-scale ML prediction, longer rollouts, data assimilation, and use for climate hazard dynamical downscaling.
- **Issues:** Regional domain with lateral and synoptic conditioning from reanalysis; trained to emulate HRRR, so it inherits HRRR biases; skill limited to short lead times.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Evaluation of five global AI models for predicting weather in Eastern Asia and Western Pacific](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41612-024-00769-0)
Liu et al. (2024), *npj Climate and Atmospheric Science*. 56 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides a homogeneous comparison of five global machine-learning weather prediction models for East Asia and the Western Pacific, including typhoon forecasts.
- **Architecture:** Benchmark evaluation of existing models: Pangu-Weather (transformer), FourCastNet v2 (spherical Fourier neural operator), GraphCast (graph neural network), FuXi and FengWu (transformer-based), plus a simple multi-model ensemble mean.
- **Data:** All models initialised from identical ERA5 initial conditions; evaluation June–November 2023 over Eastern Asia and Western Pacific, including 11 typhoons of 2023 and a Typhoon Haikui case study.
- **Main result:** FengWu performs best, followed by FuXi and GraphCast, with FCN2 and Pangu-Weather lower; the five-model average rivals FengWu. FengWu gives the best typhoon tracks but the largest intensity errors.
- **Open work:** Longer evaluation periods, operational initial conditions, and better typhoon intensity prediction from AI models.
- **Issues:** Single season of evaluation and few typhoons; ERA5 initial conditions are not available in real time; intensity is systematically underestimated by coarse AI models.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [FengWu-GHR: Learning the Kilometer-scale Medium-range Global Weather Forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.00059)
Han et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 52 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a data-driven global medium-range forecast model at kilometer-scale resolution beyond the 0.25° limit of reanalysis-trained models.
- **Architecture:** Transformer-based FengWu-family model that inherits knowledge from a pretrained low-resolution (0.25°) model and is adapted to 0.09° resolution.
- **Data:** Low-resolution pretraining on ERA5; high-resolution training on ECMWF operational analysis at about 0.09°. Hindcasts for 2022 and station observations used for evaluation.
- **Main result:** Running at 0.09°, FengWu-GHR is reported superior to IFS-HRES in 2022 hindcasts and competitive against station observations and in extreme-event case studies.
- **Open work:** Operational deployment, coupling with high-resolution data assimilation, and further resolution increases.
- **Issues:** High-resolution training data cover a short period; skill against own-type analysis may favor the model; effective resolution and small-scale realism are not fully demonstrated.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

Abraham et al. (2001), *Venue not recorded*. 52 citations.

Hansen et al. (2001), *Venue not recorded*. 51 citations.

Gao et al. (2025), *International Conference on Machine Learning*. 50 citations.

- **Data:** Reanalysis data, presumably ERA5, for global forecasts plus regional high-resolution data; exact datasets and periods are not given in the abstract.

Williams (1997), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 49 citations.

Alexe et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 48 citations.

Kittredge et al. (1986), *International Conference on Computational Linguistics*. 47 citations.

Ingsrisawang et al. (2008), *World Academy of Science, Engineering and Technology, International Journal of Computer, Electrical, Automation, Control and Information Engineering*. 46 citations.

Ware et al. (2006), *Weather and Forecasting*. 44 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves snowfall forecasts by accounting for climatological variability of snow density instead of a fixed 10:1 snow-to-liquid ratio.

### [Towards physically consistent data-driven weather forecasting: Integrating data assimilation with equivariance-preserving deep spatial transformers](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-2021-71)
Chattopadhyay et al. (2021), *arXiv*. 42 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves physical consistency and accuracy of data-driven weather prediction and integrates it with data assimilation.

- **Main result:** U-STNs outperform U-Nets (e.g., 45% skill improvement); DA cycles are stable with high observation noise using O(1000) ensembles, and multi-time-step DA reduces errors by factors of 2–3.

- **Issues:** Single-variable Z500 setup at coarse resolution; short-term forecasts only, with idealized observations.

Chen et al. (2023), *arXiv*. 38 citations.

Rogers (1989), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 36 citations.

Husain et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 35 citations.

- **Main result:** GraphCast large scales beat GEM at longer leads; the hybrid improves GEM skill, keeps a full power spectrum and physically consistent fields, and improves tropical cyclone tracks without changing intensity.

Xu et al. (2024), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 32 citations.

- **Data:** Doppler LIDAR radial velocity data; site and period not reported.

- **Open work:** Comparison with standard neural networks and extrapolation methods on more cases.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; limited cases and unknown skill.

### [THE FORECAST ICING POTENTIAL ALGORITHM](https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2004-231)
Mcdonough et al. (2004), *Venue not recorded*. 20 citations.

### [Artificial neural networks in weather forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1109/rnns.1992.268635)
Diyankov et al. (1992), *[Proceedings] 1992 RNNS/IEEE Symposium on Neuroinformatics and Neurocomputers*. 19 citations.

- **Main goal:** Applies artificial neural networks to weather forecasting as an alternative to statistical methods.

### [Dynamical Recurrent Neural Networks and Pattern Recognition Methods for Time Series Prediction - Application to Seeing and Temperature Forecasting in the Context of Eso's VLT Astronomical Weather Station](https://doi.org/10.1016/0083-6656(94)90047-7)
Aussem et al. (1994), *Vistas in Astronomy*. 18 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts astronomical seeing and temperature for ESO's Very Large Telescope site to aid observation scheduling and telescope operation.
- **Architecture:** Dynamical recurrent neural networks (time-delay recurrent networks) compared with pattern recognition methods such as nearest-neighbour time series prediction.
- **Data:** Time series from the astronomical weather station at the VLT site (Cerro Paranal); exact record length not reported here.
- **Main result:** Reports short-term predictability of temperature and seeing with recurrent networks; specific error values are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Longer records, additional meteorological predictors and operational deployment for scheduling.
- **Issues:** Seeing is highly variable and only partly predictable from local station data; limited data length and site-specific results.
