- **Issues:** Tested only on Lorenz-96; training relies on analysis fields from conventional methods.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Learning to Infer Weather States Using Partial Observations](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024jh000260)
Chao et al. (2025), *Journal of Geophysical Research*. 17 citations.

- **Main goal:** Uses the low-dimensional climatological structure of atmospheric circulation as a prior for estimating weather states from sparse observations and designing observation networks.
- **Architecture:** Deep generative model learning the climatological distribution, combined with station observations for Bayesian posterior state estimation; specific generative family not stated in the abstract.
- **Data:** Climate reanalysis or simulation output for training; case study of 2 m temperature spatial patterns with few station observations.
- **Main result:** Learned prior reproduces climatology statistics; posterior estimates are spatially coherent, adaptive to observations and uncertainty-aware, enabling ranking of observation value.
- **Open work:** Extend to multivariate, three-dimensional states and to operational observation network design.
- **Issues:** Demonstrated only for 2 m temperature patterns; trained on reanalysis or simulations so inherits their biases.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Data Assimilation with Machine Learning Surrogate Models: A Case Study with FourCastNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13180)
Adrian et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 17 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether ML weather surrogates, unstable for long rollouts, can support accurate long-term state estimation when combined with sparse noisy observations.
- **Architecture:** FourCastNet (Fourier neural operator based surrogate) integrated in a variational data assimilation framework, with theoretical analysis of filtering stability.
- **Data:** Partial, noisy synthetic observations from ERA5.
- **Main result:** Filtering estimates remain accurate over a year-long assimilation window and provide effective initial conditions for forecasts, including extreme events.
- **Open work:** Test with real observing systems and other surrogates, and compare with operational assimilation.
- **Issues:** Uses synthetic observations from ERA5 rather than real observations; idealized setting relative to operational DA.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Global Atmospheric Data Assimilation with Multi-Modal Masked Autoencoders](https://doi.org/10.1109/icdmw69685.2025.00103)
Vandal et al. (2024), *2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops (ICDMW)*. 17 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces a global gap-filled atmospheric state directly from multi-modal satellite observations as a fast AI alternative to operational data assimilation.
- **Architecture:** EarthNet, a multi-modal foundation model based on masked autoencoders that ingests a 12-hour sequence of satellite observations and learns to fill missing data across sensors.
- **Data:** Multi-modal satellite observations; evaluated against MERRA2 and ERA5 reanalyses and Microwave integrated Retrieval System (MiRS) retrievals.
- **Main result:** Generates a 0.16 degree 3D temperature and humidity state in 5 minutes on one GPU (50x faster than operational systems); 3D humidity beats MERRA2 and ERA5 by 10-60% at 5-20 km but underperforms near the surface and for temperature.
- **Open work:** Use EarthNet for high-frequency data assimilation and as initial conditions for global weather forecasting.
- **Issues:** Weaker near-surface and temperature performance; evaluated partly against retrievals; no dynamical consistency constraints or forecast-skill impact shown.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [FNP: Fourier Neural Processes for Arbitrary-Resolution Data Assimilation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.01645)
Chen et al. (2024), *Neural Information Processing Systems*. 17 citations.

- **Main goal:** Enables AI-based data assimilation that can ingest observations at arbitrary and varying resolutions rather than a single fixed one.
- **Architecture:** Fourier Neural Processes (FNP), a neural process framework with Fourier-based modules for resolution-agnostic assimilation of background forecasts and observations.
- **Data:** Not reported in the abstract; global medium-range weather fields with observations at varying resolutions.
- **Main result:** FNP achieves state-of-the-art assimilation across resolutions, with growing advantage as resolution and observation amount increase, and generalizes to unseen resolutions and to observation reconstruction without fine-tuning.
- **Open work:** Test with real, irregular operational observations and in cycled assimilation-forecast systems.
- **Issues:** Likely synthetic observations derived from gridded data; real observation operators, errors and cycling are not addressed in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [AI-based data assimilation: Learning the functional of analysis estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00390)
Keller et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 16 citations.

- **Main goal:** Replaces classical variational data assimilation with a neural network that directly learns the analysis functional, without requiring pre-existing analysis datasets.
- **Architecture:** AI-Var: a neural network trained to minimize the variational (3D-Var-type) cost function, mapping background and observations to an analysis; network family is not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Idealized test cases and real-world test cases with NWP backgrounds and observations; specific products are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Proof of concept shows AI-Var can efficiently assimilate observations and produce accurate initial conditions for NWP.
- **Open work:** Scale to full operational observation sets and integrate into fully data-driven NWP systems.
- **Issues:** Proof-of-concept only; quantitative comparisons with operational DA are not given; handling of complex observation operators and error covariances unclear.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [PhyDA: Physics-Guided Diffusion Models for Data Assimilation in Atmospheric Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.12882)
Wang et al. (2025), *arXiv*. 15 citations.

- **Main goal:** Makes diffusion-model-based atmospheric data assimilation physically consistent, since purely data-driven reconstructions can violate governing dynamics and harm downstream use.
- **Architecture:** PhyDA, a physics-guided diffusion model with a physically regularized diffusion objective penalizing PDE residuals and a Virtual Reconstruction Encoder mapping sparse observations to structured latent representations.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis with sparse synthetic observations; details on resolution, variables and periods are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Achieves higher reconstruction accuracy and better physical plausibility than state-of-the-art data assimilation baselines.
- **Open work:** Apply the approach to real observing systems and operational data assimilation, and extend the set of physical constraints.
- **Issues:** Evaluated on ERA5 with simulated observations rather than real observation streams; physical constraints are approximate PDE penalties, not hard guarantees.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [4D‐Var Using Hessian Approximation and Backpropagation Applied to Automatically Differentiable Numerical and Machine Learning Models](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024ms004608)
Solvik et al. (2024), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 14 citations.

- **Main goal:** Simplifies 4D-Var data assimilation by avoiding hand-written tangent linear and adjoint models when the forecast model supports automatic differentiation.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML data assimilation method: 4D-Var approximating Gauss-Newton via backpropagation combined with a Hessian approximation, applicable to autodiff physical models or ML surrogate models.
- **Data:** Idealized Lorenz-96 and quasi-geostrophic models with synthetic observations.
- **Main result:** The approach is efficient and in some cases more accurate than incremental 4D-Var.
- **Open work:** Integrate with operational-scale differentiable weather models and ML surrogates in next-generation forecast systems.
- **Issues:** Tested only on idealized low-dimensional systems; scalability and robustness with real observations and full NWP models remain undemonstrated.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Interpretable Structural Model Error Discovery From Sparse Assimilation Increments Using Spectral Bias‐Reduced Neural Networks: A Quasi‐Geostrophic Turbulence Test Case](https://doi.org/10.1029/2023ms004033)
Mojgani et al. (2023), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 14 citations.

- **Main goal:** Discovers interpretable structural and parametric model errors from sparse data assimilation increments, an alternative to opaque neural network nudging corrections.
- **Architecture:** MEDIDA: sparsity-promoting equation discovery on analysis increments, with a neural network interpolator augmented by a random Fourier feature layer to reduce spectral bias.
- **Data:** Two-layer quasi-geostrophic turbulence simulations with full and spatially sparse synthetic observations.
- **Main result:** MEDIDA recovers linear and nonlinear model errors with full observations; plain neural network interpolators fail with sparse data due to spectral bias, but the random Fourier feature layer fixes this.
- **Open work:** Scale MEDIDA to Earth system models and real observations.
- **Issues:** Idealized QG test case with synthetic observations; requires very accurate interpolation; real-data robustness untested.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Using data assimilation tools to dissect GraphDOP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27388)
Laloyaux et al. (2025), *arXiv*. 11 citations.

- **Main goal:** Transfers data assimilation diagnostics such as Forecast Sensitivity-based Observation Impact (FSOI) to machine-learning weather models to make the observation-driven GraphDOP model interpretable and explainable.
- **Architecture:** Graph neural network (GraphDOP, ECMWF) with a sliding attention window, analysed through adjoint-style sensitivities obtained by automatic differentiation; FSOI computed via gradients of forecast error.
- **Data:** Conventional in-situ and satellite observations ingested directly by GraphDOP at ECMWF; no reanalysis input. Specific periods not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The attention window learns meteorological features and spatial relationships, e.g. storm-system movement; FSOI shows GraphDOP builds an internal Earth-system representation combining conventional and satellite observations.
- **Open work:** Using these diagnostics to guide observing-system design and model development for observation-driven ML forecasting, and comparing ML and NWP observation impacts.
- **Issues:** Mainly qualitative case-based diagnostics; gradient-based sensitivities of a neural network may be noisy and do not guarantee physical causality.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A novel latent space data assimilation framework with Autoencoder-Observation to Latent space (AE-O2L) network. Part I: the observation-only analysis method](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-24-0057.1)
Fan et al. (2025), *Monthly Weather Review*. 9 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces the computational burden of data assimilation by performing analysis in a learned latent space directly from observations.
- **Architecture:** Autoencoder learning a latent space of atmospheric states plus O2Lnet, a neural network mapping observations into the latent space, decoded to obtain the analysis (LSDA-OOA).
- **Data:** WRF-FDDA analyses (and alternatively forecasts) for training; idealized and real 2 m temperature observations on 1 km grids.
- **Main result:** LSDA-OOA yields high-quality T2 analyses robust to observation errors, comparable to WRF-FDDA accuracy and much better when background forecasts have large errors.
- **Open work:** Part II of the series combining background information; extension to more variables and 3D fields.
- **Issues:** Only 2 m temperature tested; observation-only analysis needs sufficient observations; performance tied to WRF training data.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Machine Learning for Targeted Assimilation of Satellite Data](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-10997-4_4)
Lee et al. (2018), *ECML/PKDD*. 9 citations.

- **Main goal:** Uses machine learning to target which satellite observations to assimilate, reducing the cost of ingesting very large satellite data volumes in data assimilation.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning to identify regions or features of interest for targeted assimilation; the model family is not specified here.
- **Data:** Satellite observations for NWP data assimilation; specific instruments and models not reported (no abstract).
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Demonstrating forecast impact of targeted assimilation in an operational data assimilation system.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; card is inferred from the title and should be checked.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Four‐Dimensional Variational Informed Generative Adversarial Network for Data Assimilation](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024ms004437)
Wang et al. (2025), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Accelerates 4DVar data assimilation for data-driven weather prediction while keeping analyses accurate and stable.
- **Architecture:** 4DVarGAN: conditional generative adversarial network solving the 4DVar cost function non-iteratively, with cycle-consistent adversarial data augmentation and 4DVar-based adaptive adjustment.
- **Data:** WeatherBench 500 hPa geopotential fields.
- **Main result:** 73-fold acceleration versus 4DVar with the DDWP model, lowest analysis and forecast errors among DL-based DA methods, and stable results across background qualities.
- **Open work:** Extension to multivariate, 3D and real observation settings.
- **Issues:** Single variable (Z500) at coarse resolution; simulated observations; idealized relative to operational DA.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Four-dimensional variational data assimilation with a sea-ice thickness emulator](https://doi.org/10.5194/tc-19-5613-2025)
Durand et al. (2025), *The Cryosphere*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a variational data assimilation system for Arctic sea-ice thickness, since the neXtSIM brittle-rheology sea-ice model has no adjoint for 4D-Var.
- **Architecture:** Neural network emulator of neXtSIM sea-ice thickness (convolutional, U-Net-like) whose automatic-differentiation adjoint drives a 4D-Var system, testing two background covariance approximations.
- **Data:** Arctic-wide neXtSIM mesoscale (~10 km) simulations for emulator training; twin experiments plus assimilation of real CS2SMOS satellite thickness retrievals; comparison with operational neXtSIM-F forecasts.
- **Main result:** Twin experiments reduce sea-ice thickness RMSE by 0.8 m on average versus the free run and improve marginal ice zone positioning; with CS2SMOS the system corrects forecast bias and matches neXtSIM-F performance.
- **Open work:** Extend to more variables (concentration, drift), assimilate higher-resolution observations, and refine background covariance modelling for emulator-based 4D-Var.
- **Issues:** Assimilating smooth CS2SMOS retrievals amplifies loss of small-scale information; emulator covers thickness only and inherits neXtSIM biases; the adjoint is that of the emulator, not the physical model.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Evaluating Machine Learning Weather Models for Data Assimilation: Fundamental Limitations in Tangent Linear and Adjoint Properties](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025gl119402)
Tian et al. (2026), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses whether ML weather models have physically meaningful tangent linear and adjoint properties required for data assimilation.
- **Architecture:** Evaluation of tangent linear and adjoint models of GraphCast (graph neural network) and NeuralGCM (hybrid differentiable dynamical core with neural network physics) versus the MPAS-A numerical model.
- **Data:** Perturbation response experiments with GraphCast, NeuralGCM and MPAS-A; specific initial conditions not detailed in the abstract.
- **Main result:** ML models show unphysical adjoint sensitivities, persistent localized responses and excessive noise, unlike physically consistent MPAS-A patterns.
- **Open work:** Improve linearization properties of ML weather models before operational DA use.
- **Issues:** Only two ML models tested; implications for DA systems are inferred rather than demonstrated in cycled assimilation.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Unified Neural Background‐Error Covariance Model for Midlatitude and Tropical Atmospheric Data Assimilation](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025ms005360)
Melinc et al. (2025), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 4 citations.

- **Main goal:** Model background-error covariances for variational data assimilation that respect physical balances in both midlatitudes and tropics, where standard balance operators are poorly suited.
- **Architecture:** Neural-network autoencoder whose reduced latent space is used to estimate background-error covariances and perform variational data assimilation in latent space.
- **Data:** Autoencoder trained on 40 years of ERA5 reanalysis; single-observation experiments (500 hPa geopotential, total column water vapour) and tests with synthetic and operational ensembles of data assimilations.
- **Main result:** Latent-space DA produces localized, flow-dependent increments consistent with geostrophic and thermal-wind balance in midlatitudes and heating-induced responses in the tropics; forecasts from these analyses evolve realistically, including a Kelvin wave.
- **Open work:** Developing ensemble-based latent-space 4D-Var and full cycling experiments with real observations.
- **Issues:** Autoencoder compression causes significant variance loss in some variables; demonstrations rely mainly on single-observation and idealized experiments.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [ADAF: An Artificial Intelligence Data Assimilation Framework for Weather Forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024ms004839)
Xiang et al. (2025), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 1 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a fast AI-based data assimilation framework to produce kilometre-scale near-surface analyses from real multi-source observations at low computational cost.
- **Architecture:** ADAF: a deep learning data assimilation framework that maps a background field plus sparse observations to an analysis; network family not specified in the abstract.
- **Data:** Real-world sparse surface weather observations and satellite imagery over CONUS for four near-surface variables; compared with HRRRDAS-initialized forecasts.
- **Main result:** Analyses align closely with observations, reconstruct extremes such as tropical cyclone wind fields, remain good with poor backgrounds and very sparse observations, run in about 2 s on an AMD MI200 GPU, and improve 0–6 h AI forecasts over HRRRDAS initialization.
- **Open work:** Extending to more variables, upper-air fields and operational cycling with forecast models.
- **Issues:** Limited to four near-surface variables over CONUS; verification partly against the same observation types assimilated; no explicit uncertainty estimate.
- *Basis: abstract*

<a id="remote_sensing"></a>
## Remote sensing & clouds

### [Deep learning in remote sensing: a review](https://doi.org/10.1109/mgrs.2017.2762307)
Zhu et al. (2017), *arXiv*. 2,000 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses the challenges and opportunities of deep learning for remote sensing data analysis and lowers the barrier for remote sensing scientists to adopt it.
- **Architecture:** Review of deep learning for remote sensing, mainly convolutional neural networks (CNN) and related deep architectures for classification, detection, fusion and retrieval tasks.
- **Data:** No new data; surveys remote sensing applications across hyperspectral, SAR, optical and other imagery, and lists datasets and resources.
- **Main result:** Argues that deep learning is a powerful but not universal tool, and that domain expertise must be combined with it to tackle large-scale problems.
- **Open work:** Advocates applying deep learning to large-scale challenges such as climate change and urbanization, with remote sensing knowledge built in.
- **Issues:** Survey of a fast-moving field as of 2017; little coverage of atmospheric or oceanic applications specifically.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Evaluation of PERSIANN system satellite-based estimates of tropical rainfall](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0477(2000)081<2035:eopsse>2.3.co;2)
Sorooshian et al. (2000), *Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society*. 1,241 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates the PERSIANN satellite rainfall estimation system over the tropics to assess the accuracy of neural-network-based precipitation estimates.
- **Architecture:** PERSIANN neural network (modified counterpropagation network with a self-organizing feature map layer) mapping geostationary infrared brightness temperatures to rain rate, adaptively updated with microwave rainfall.
- **Data:** Geostationary infrared imagery with TRMM microwave rainfall for adjustment; validation against TRMM products, radar and rain-gauge observations in the tropics.
- **Main result:** PERSIANN estimates agree reasonably with independent observations, with accuracy improving at coarser space and time aggregation.
- **Open work:** Improving fine-scale accuracy and extending evaluation to other regions and seasons.
- **Issues:** Infrared-based estimates relate only indirectly to surface rain; detailed error statistics are not given here.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information Using Artificial Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1997)036<1176:pefrsi>2.0.co;2)
Hsu et al. (1997), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 1,082 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall rate from satellite infrared imagery to provide precipitation fields where gauges and radar are sparse (the PERSIANN system).
- **Architecture:** Modified counterpropagation artificial neural network: a self-organizing feature map that classifies inputs followed by a Grossberg linear output layer, with adaptive online updating of parameters.
- **Data:** Geostationary infrared brightness temperatures with surface-derived input features, trained and validated against rain gauge and radar rainfall over test regions.
- **Main result:** The network produces rainfall estimates at hourly and fine spatial resolution that compare favorably with other satellite techniques and improve when parameters are updated with ground observations.
- **Open work:** Incorporation of microwave data, global extension and continued adaptive calibration.
- **Issues:** Infrared signals relate only indirectly to surface rain; skill depends on regime and on availability of ground truth for updating.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Imagery Using an Artificial Neural Network Cloud Classification System](https://doi.org/10.1175/jam2173.1)
Hong et al. (2004), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 794 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall from satellite infrared imagery at high resolution by classifying cloud patches and assigning cloud-type-specific rain rates (PERSIANN-CCS).
- **Architecture:** Cloud classification system: segmentation of infrared cloud images into patches, feature extraction, a self-organizing map (SOM) neural network to cluster patches, and per-cluster temperature-rain rate curves.
- **Data:** Geostationary GOES infrared imagery, calibrated and validated against ground radar rainfall estimates.
- **Main result:** Produces rainfall estimates at finer resolution than earlier PERSIANN, with better skill from distinguishing cloud types; exact scores not given here.
- **Open work:** Adding multispectral and passive microwave information and extending coverage.
- **Issues:** Abstract not available; relies on knowledge of the paper. IR-only inputs relate cloud-top temperature to rainfall only indirectly.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Classification of snow cover and precipitation using the special sensor microwave imager](https://doi.org/10.1029/91jd00045)
Grody (1991), *Journal of Geophysical Research*. 496 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies snow cover and precipitation from passive microwave observations to support global monitoring.
- **Architecture:** Physically based decision tree (threshold-based screening) classification using microwave brightness temperatures; not a learned model.
- **Data:** DMSP Special Sensor Microwave/Imager (SSM/I) brightness temperatures at multiple frequencies.
- **Main result:** Develops a decision-tree classifier that separates snow cover, precipitation and other surfaces such as cold deserts and frozen ground.
- **Open work:** Quantitative snow and rain retrieval and better handling of ambiguous surfaces.
- **Issues:** Confusion with surfaces of similar scattering signatures; thresholds may be region dependent.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [The Hydrometeor Classification Algorithm for the Polarimetric WSR-88D: Description and Application to an MCS](https://doi.org/10.1175/2008waf2222205.1)
Park et al. (2009), *Weather and Forecasting*. 482 citations.

- **Main goal:** Describes a hydrometeor classification algorithm for the polarimetric WSR-88D radar network.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classification of radar echoes into hydrometeor and non-meteorological classes.
- **Data:** Polarimetric radar data (KOUN, Oklahoma) for a mesoscale convective system.
- **Main result:** The algorithm discriminates about ten classes and produces plausible microphysical structure for the MCS.
- **Open work:** Validation against in situ observations and operational implementation.
- **Issues:** Membership functions are prescribed; limited verification.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A cloud detection algorithm for satellite imagery based on deep learning](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2019.03.039)
Jeppesen et al. (2019), *Remote Sensing of Environment*. 387 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detect clouds in optical satellite imagery using spatial context, reducing misclassification over bright surfaces such as snow and ice.
- **Architecture:** RS-Net, a U-Net based convolutional segmentation network; also trained with noisy Fmask labels.
- **Data:** Landsat 8 Biome and SPARCS cloud-mask datasets, plus Fmask-generated annotations.
- **Main result:** State-of-the-art performance especially over snow/ice; RGB-only models perform well; training on Fmask labels yields better masks than Fmask itself; classifying a full Landsat 8 scene takes about 18 s.
- **Open work:** Application to small satellites with limited bands and to other sensors.
- **Issues:** Evaluated on limited labeled datasets; cloud shadow and thin cloud handling not detailed in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Classification of Hydrometeors Based on Polarimetric Radar Measurements: Development of Fuzzy Logic and Neuro-Fuzzy Systems, and In Situ Verification](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(2000)017<0140:cohbop>2.0.co;2)
Liu et al. (2000), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 385 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies hydrometeor types from polarimetric radar measurements and verifies the classification with in situ observations.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classification system and a neuro-fuzzy system (a neural network trained to tune fuzzy membership functions).
- **Data:** Polarimetric radar observations from the CSU-CHILL radar, with in situ aircraft observations for verification.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy and neuro-fuzzy classifiers produce hydrometeor classes consistent with in situ observations.
- **Open work:** More extensive verification datasets and adaptation to other radars and climates.
- **Issues:** Limited verification cases; membership functions depend on radar frequency and calibration.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Radiometric profiling of temperature, water vapor and cloud liquid water using various inversion methods](https://doi.org/10.1029/97rs03656)
Solheim et al. (1998), *Radio Science*. 292 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves vertical profiles of temperature, water vapour and cloud liquid water from ground-based multichannel microwave radiometer observations.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of inversion methods including statistical regression, a neural network and physical iterative (Bayesian/Newtonian) retrievals.
- **Data:** Ground-based microwave radiometer brightness temperatures with radiosonde profiles for training and validation.
- **Main result:** Profiles are retrieved with useful accuracy in the lower troposphere, with neural network and regression methods performing comparably; details not reproduced here.
- **Open work:** Combining radiometry with other sensors to improve vertical resolution and cloud liquid retrieval.
- **Issues:** Vertical resolution degrades with height; statistical retrievals depend on the representativeness of the radiosonde training climatology.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Global identification of snowcover using SSM/I measurements](https://doi.org/10.1109/36.481908)
Grody et al. (1996), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 286 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies snow cover globally from passive microwave measurements, separating snow from other scattering surfaces such as precipitation, cold desert and frozen ground.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML decision-tree (threshold) algorithm based on scattering indices from multiple SSM/I channels.
- **Data:** SSM/I brightness temperatures with comparisons against snow cover analyses.
- **Main result:** The algorithm identifies global snow cover consistent with independent snow maps while screening out confounding scatterers.
- **Open work:** Retrieval of snow depth or water equivalent and improved detection of shallow and wet snow.
- **Issues:** Misses shallow and wet snow; coarse resolution and threshold choices limit accuracy in some regions.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A neural network approach to cloud classification](https://doi.org/10.1109/36.58972)
Lee et al. (1990), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 285 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies cloud types in satellite imagery using neural networks applied to textural features.
- **Architecture:** Backpropagation neural network (multilayer perceptron) using texture features, compared with statistical classifiers.
- **Data:** Landsat Multispectral Scanner imagery samples of stratocumulus, cumulus and cirrus clouds.
- **Main result:** The neural network achieves high classification accuracy, exceeding traditional statistical classification methods.
- **Open work:** Larger and more varied training samples and more cloud classes.
- **Issues:** Small sample of scenes; classes limited to a few cloud types; texture features from one sensor.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A new neural network approach including first guess for retrieval of atmospheric water vapor, cloud liquid water path, surface temperature, and emissivities over land from satellite microwave observations](https://doi.org/10.1029/2001jd900085)
Aires et al. (2001), *Journal of Geophysical Research*. 259 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves atmospheric water vapor, cloud liquid water path, surface temperature and microwave emissivities over land, where variable surface emissivity hampers retrievals.
- **Architecture:** Neural network inversion that uses a first-guess estimate as additional input to regularize the retrieval.
- **Data:** SSM/I satellite microwave observations with first-guess information from ancillary datasets (e.g. ISCCP and TOVS-type products).
- **Main result:** Including the first guess substantially improves retrieval accuracy over land compared with a network without it.
- **Open work:** Applying to other sensors and global, long-term processing.
- **Issues:** Accuracy depends on first-guess quality; training relies on simulated or ancillary data with their own biases.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Survey on Gaussian Processes for Earth-Observation Data Analysis: A Comprehensive Investigation](https://doi.org/10.1109/mgrs.2015.2510084)
Camps-Valls et al. (2016), *IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine*. 257 citations.

- **Main goal:** Surveys Gaussian processes for Earth observation data analysis, motivated by their accuracy, uncertainty estimates and interpretability for retrieving biophysical parameters.
- **Architecture:** Review and tutorial of Gaussian process regression for remote sensing, including kernel design, model inversion, emulation of radiative transfer models, and scalable/heteroscedastic variants.
- **Data:** Illustrative examples on optical and other remote sensing data for biophysical parameter retrieval (e.g., vegetation variables); details not given here.
- **Main result:** Gaussian processes are shown to be accurate and flexible for EO parameter estimation, offering uncertainty and interpretable kernel hyperparameters.
- **Open work:** Scaling GPs to big EO data, multi-output and physically consistent GPs, and wider operational use.
- **Issues:** Survey from 2016; GP computational cost limits large datasets; details not verified because the abstract is unavailable.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Intercomparison of rain gauge, radar, and satellite-based precipitation estimates with emphasis on hydrologic forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1175/jhm431.1)
Yilmaz et al. (2005), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 256 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares rain gauge, radar and satellite mean areal precipitation estimates and their value for hydrologic forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Not an ML method itself: comparison study that evaluates the PERSIANN neural-network satellite precipitation product and drives the SAC-SMA conceptual hydrologic model.
- **Data:** Gauge MAP (MAPG), radar/gauge multisensor MAP (MAPX) and PERSIANN satellite MAP (MAPS), March 2000 to November 2003, seven basins in the southeastern United States.
- **Main result:** Agreement between datasets varies strongly across basins and in time; PERSIANN-driven flows depend on calibration, with recalibration on satellite data improving simulations.
- **Open work:** Bias correction of satellite estimates and assessment in more basins and climates.
- **Issues:** Short record; satellite estimates show basin-dependent biases; lumped model only.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Retrieval of land surface albedo from satellite observations: a simulation study](https://doi.org/10.1109/igarss.1998.691379)
Liang et al. (1998), *IGARSS '98. Sensing and Managing the Environment. 1998 IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing. Symposium Proceedings. (Cat. No.98CH36174)*. 252 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses, through simulations, how well land surface albedo can be retrieved from satellite observations.
- **Architecture:** Retrieval algorithms developed from radiative transfer simulations; the specific inversion method is not reliably known here.
- **Data:** Simulated surface and top-of-atmosphere reflectances from radiative transfer models.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Validation with real satellite data and field albedo measurements.
- **Issues:** Simulation-only study, so performance depends on the realism of the modeled surfaces and atmospheres.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Use of Three-Dimensional Reflectivity Structure for Automated Detection and Removal of Nonprecipitating Echoes in Radar Data](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(2002)019<0673:uotdrs>2.0.co;2)
Steiner et al. (2002), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 252 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automatically detects and removes non-precipitating echoes (ground clutter, anomalous propagation) from weather radar data.
- **Architecture:** Rule-based (non-ML) algorithm using three-dimensional reflectivity structure (echo depth, vertical gradient and spatial variability) with decision thresholds.
- **Data:** Volume-scan reflectivity data from WSR-88D weather radars.
- **Main result:** The algorithm effectively removes anomalous-propagation and clutter echoes while retaining precipitation.
- **Open work:** Combining with Doppler velocity and polarimetric information.
- **Issues:** Threshold-based rules may misclassify shallow precipitation or embedded clutter.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Evaluation of PERSIANN-CCS rainfall measurement using the NAME event rain gauge network](https://doi.org/10.1175/jhm574.1)
Hong et al. (2007), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 242 citations.

- **Main goal:** Evaluates a high-resolution satellite rainfall product over complex terrain in the North American Monsoon region.
- **Architecture:** Not an ML method itself: evaluation of PERSIANN-CCS, a neural-network-based cloud-classification satellite rainfall algorithm.
- **Data:** PERSIANN-CCS estimates and the NAME event rain gauge network over the Sierra Madre Occidental, Mexico, 2004 monsoon.
- **Main result:** PERSIANN-CCS captures the diurnal cycle and spatial patterns but shows elevation-dependent biases, underestimating at high elevations.
- **Open work:** Terrain-aware corrections and combining with gauge data.
- **Issues:** Single season and region; gauge representativeness limits evaluation.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Improving Precipitation Estimation Using Convolutional Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1029/2018wr024090)
Pan et al. (2019), *Water Resources Research*. 240 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improve daily precipitation estimation via statistical downscaling from dynamically resolved variables as an alternative to precipitation parameterizations.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network learning precipitation-related features from surrounding resolved fields; architectures compared and interpreted.
- **Data:** Reanalysis dynamical fields as predictors and observed daily precipitation at 14 grid points across the contiguous US.
- **Main result:** With enough data, CNN beats reanalysis precipitation and downscaling by linear regression, nearest neighbor, random forest and fully connected networks.
- **Open work:** Using insights to improve precipitation parameterizations and integrating into NWP models.
- **Issues:** Only 14 locations; performance depends on data quantity; point-wise models rather than a spatially coherent field.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A multichannel radiometric profiler of temperature, humidity, and cloud liquid](https://doi.org/10.1029/2002rs002856)
Ware et al. (2003), *Radio Science*. 238 citations.

- **Main goal:** Describes a ground-based multichannel microwave radiometric profiler for temperature, humidity and cloud liquid profiles.
- **Architecture:** Instrument description; profiles are retrieved from radiometer brightness temperatures with neural network retrieval trained on radiosonde data.
- **Data:** Radiometer brightness temperatures with radiosonde data for training and comparison.
- **Main result:** The profiler provides continuous temperature, humidity and cloud liquid profiles in reasonable agreement with radiosondes.
- **Open work:** Combining with other sensors and data assimilation.
- **Issues:** Vertical resolution degrades with height; retrievals depend on climatological training data.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A spatiotemporal deep fusion model for merging satellite and gauge precipitation in China](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2020.124664)
Wu et al. (2020), *Journal of Hydrology*. 215 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improve quantitative precipitation estimation over China by merging satellite, gauge and infrared data while using spatial and temporal correlations together.
- **Architecture:** CNN-LSTM fusion model: CNN extracts spatial features of satellite, gauge and thermal infrared data; LSTM captures time dependence.
- **Data:** TRMM 3B42 V7, thermal infrared imagery, and 796 rain gauges in China; produces a daily 0.05° dataset for 2001-2005.
- **Main result:** Outperforms CNN, LSTM and MLP alone; reduces TRMM RMSE by 17.0% and MAE by 14.7%, raising correlation to 0.72, including for gauge-sparse regions.
- **Open work:** Extend to newer satellite products (e.g. IMERG), longer periods, and sub-daily resolution.
- **Issues:** Evaluation against gauges that also inform the merge needs careful independence; product covers only 2001-2005; extremes may be underestimated.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Estimation of physical variables from multichannel remotely sensed imagery using a neural network: Application to rainfall estimation](https://doi.org/10.1029/1999wr900032)
Hsu et al. (1999), *Water Resources Research*. 212 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall from multichannel remotely sensed imagery using neural networks.
- **Architecture:** Modified counterpropagation network combining a self-organizing feature map with a Grossberg linear output layer (the PERSIANN approach).
- **Data:** Geostationary infrared satellite imagery with ground radar or gauge rainfall data for training and validation.
- **Main result:** The network produces rainfall estimates more accurate than conventional infrared techniques.
- **Open work:** Including microwave data and online adaptive training.
- **Issues:** Infrared-based estimates are indirectly related to rainfall; performance varies by region and season.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Diurnal Variability of Tropical Rainfall Retrieved from Combined GOES and TRMM Satellite Information](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0442(2002)015<0983:dvotrr>2.0.co;2)
Sorooshian et al. (2002), *Journal of Climate*. 195 citations.

- **Main goal:** Characterizes the diurnal cycle of tropical rainfall using high-resolution satellite precipitation estimates.
- **Architecture:** PERSIANN neural-network precipitation retrieval (self-organizing feature map based) using GOES infrared imagery, adjusted with TRMM microwave rainfall.
- **Data:** GOES infrared and TRMM satellite data over the tropics for several years around 1998–2000.
- **Main result:** Rainfall shows a strong afternoon-to-evening maximum over land and an early-morning maximum over oceans, with regional variations resolved at high resolution.
- **Open work:** Extend the record and compare with model diurnal cycles.
- **Issues:** Infrared-based estimates have known biases for warm rain and cirrus; validation limited by sparse ground truth.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Theory-Based Hydrometeor Identification Algorithm for X-Band Polarimetric Radars](https://doi.org/10.1175/2009jtecha1208.1)
Dolan et al. (2009), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 190 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a hydrometeor identification algorithm for X-band polarimetric radars, which suffer from attenuation and differ from S-band.
- **Architecture:** Theory-based fuzzy logic classifier with membership functions derived from scattering simulations; not a learned ML model.
- **Data:** Scattering simulations for hydrometeor types and X-band polarimetric radar observations from the CASA network.
- **Main result:** The algorithm produces physically plausible hydrometeor classifications at X band.
- **Open work:** Validate with in situ observations and refine for attenuation correction.
- **Issues:** Limited validation; depends on scattering assumptions.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Atmospheric correction algorithm for MERIS above case‐2 waters](https://doi.org/10.1080/01431160600962574)
Schroeder et al. (2007), *International Journal of Remote Sensing*. 189 citations.

- **Main goal:** Corrects MERIS ocean colour data for atmospheric effects over optically complex case-2 coastal waters.
- **Architecture:** Neural network inversion (MLP) trained on radiative transfer simulations mapping top-of-atmosphere radiances to water-leaving reflectance and aerosol optical thickness.
- **Data:** Radiative transfer simulations for training; MERIS imagery validated with in situ reflectance and AERONET aerosol data in coastal European waters.
- **Main result:** The neural network correction retrieves reflectance and aerosol properties with improved accuracy over the standard MERIS processor in coastal waters.
- **Open work:** Extend validation to more coastal regions and turbid waters.
- **Issues:** Performance depends on simulated training ranges; limited in situ data.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Inversion for refractivity parameters from radar sea clutter](https://doi.org/10.1029/2002rs002640)
Gerstoft et al. (2003), *Radio Science*. 182 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates lower-atmosphere refractivity profiles, which control radar ducting, from radar sea clutter returns instead of direct soundings.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML inversion: a parabolic-equation propagation model fitted to clutter with a genetic algorithm global search, with posterior probability analysis for parameter uncertainty.
- **Data:** S-band SPANDAR radar sea clutter collected at Wallops Island, Virginia, compared with helicopter/in situ refractivity measurements.
- **Main result:** Inverted refractivity parameters reproduce the observed ducting structure and propagation loss reasonably well, demonstrating refractivity-from-clutter feasibility.
- **Open work:** Range-dependent environments, faster inversion for real-time use and more realistic clutter models.
- **Issues:** Relies on a simple parametric duct model and assumed clutter statistics; limited cases evaluated.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [An Automated Technique to Quality Control Radar Reflectivity Data](https://doi.org/10.1175/jam2460.1)
Lakshmanan et al. (2007), *Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology*. 182 citations.

- **Main goal:** Removes non-precipitating echoes such as ground clutter, anomalous propagation and biological targets from weather radar reflectivity automatically.
- **Architecture:** MLP neural network classifying radar gates using local reflectivity, velocity and spectrum-width texture and vertical-structure features, with pre- and post-processing rules.
- **Data:** WSR-88D (NEXRAD) volume scans with human-edited quality-controlled reflectivity as truth.
- **Main result:** The neural network quality control removes most contaminated echoes while preserving precipitation better than the operational WSR-88D algorithm.
- **Open work:** Using dual-polarization variables and handling clear-air and smaller precipitation echoes better.
- **Issues:** Truth relies on subjective human editing; some light precipitation and strong clutter cases remain misclassified.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### Feature Selection for Case-Based Classification of Cloud Types: An Empirical Comparison
Aha et al. (1994), *Venue not recorded*. 181 citations.

- **Main goal:** Examines which features matter for classifying cloud types in satellite imagery with case-based learning, where irrelevant features degrade performance.
- **Architecture:** Case-based (k-nearest neighbour, instance-based) classifier combined with sequential feature selection algorithms (forward and backward selection, beam search variants) in an empirical comparison.
- **Data:** Labelled AVHRR cloud samples with many spectral and textural features compiled by Bankert; sample counts not reported here.
- **Main result:** Feature selection substantially reduces the feature set while maintaining or improving classification accuracy, with backward-style search tending to perform well.
- **Open work:** Comparison with other classifiers and more efficient feature selection for large feature sets.
- **Issues:** Results depend on a single expert-labelled cloud dataset; feature search is computationally expensive and may overfit the evaluation data.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A study of cloud classification with neural networks using spectral and textural features](https://doi.org/10.1109/72.737500)
Tian et al. (1999), *IEEE Trans. Neural Networks*. 181 citations.

- **Main goal:** Studies cloud classification from multispectral geostationary satellite imagery and which spectral and textural features best separate cloud types.
- **Architecture:** Neural network classifiers applied to spectral features and textural features (e.g., gray-level co-occurrence and transform-based texture measures), compared across feature sets.
- **Data:** GOES-8 multispectral imagery with expert-labelled cloud samples; exact sample sizes not reported here.
- **Main result:** Combining spectral and textural features improves classification accuracy over spectral features alone; specific accuracy figures not reported here.
- **Open work:** Adding temporal information and testing over more regions and seasons.
- **Issues:** Depends on subjective expert labels and a limited set of scenes; generalization to other sensors and regions is untested.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Identification of hydrometeors and other targets by dual‐polarization radar](https://doi.org/10.1029/rs019i001p00132)
Hall et al. (1984), *Radio Science*. 177 citations.

- **Main goal:** Uses dual-polarization radar measurements to identify hydrometeor types and other radar targets, improving interpretation of precipitation echoes.
- **Architecture:** Non-ML method: interpretation of reflectivity and differential reflectivity (ZDR) signatures to discriminate rain, hail, snow, melting layer and non-meteorological targets.
- **Data:** Dual-polarization S-band observations from the Chilbolton radar in southern England.
- **Main result:** Differential reflectivity combined with reflectivity distinguishes rain, ice and hail regions and non-meteorological echoes such as clutter and aircraft.
- **Open work:** Quantitative, automated classification schemes and validation with in situ hydrometeor observations.
- **Issues:** Largely qualitative case-based identification without systematic in situ verification; ambiguities remain between some ice types.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [PERSIANN-CNN: Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information Using Artificial Neural Networks–Convolutional Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/jhm-d-19-0110.1)
Sadeghi et al. (2019), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 176 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improve satellite-based precipitation rate estimation using deep learning on geostationary imagery.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network (encoder-decoder) using infrared and water vapor channels from GOES.
- **Data:** Summers 2012 and 2013 over central CONUS at 0.08 deg and hourly scale; NCEP Stage IV gauge-radar as reference.
- **Main result:** PERSIANN-CNN beats PERSIANN-CCS and PERSIANN-SDAE by 54% and 23% in CSI and reduces RMSE by 37% and 14%.
- **Open work:** Extension to other seasons, regions and additional channels; operational implementation.
- **Issues:** Evaluated only for warm-season central CONUS; IR/WV channels sense cloud tops, limiting skill for some rain types.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A Fuzzy Logic Algorithm for the Separation of Precipitating from Nonprecipitating Echoes Using Polarimetric Radar Observations](https://doi.org/10.1175/jtech2035.1)
Gourley et al. (2007), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 176 citations.

- **Main goal:** Separates precipitating from nonprecipitating radar echoes such as ground clutter, sea clutter and clear-air returns using polarimetry.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classifier with membership functions derived from observed distributions of polarimetric variables and their texture.
- **Data:** C-band polarimetric radar observations from the Météo-France Trappes radar near Paris.
- **Main result:** The fuzzy logic algorithm identifies precipitation and clutter echoes with high accuracy, with differential phase texture and copolar correlation most useful.
- **Open work:** Extending to other radars, wavelengths and mixed echo situations.
- **Issues:** Membership functions are tuned to one radar; attenuation and partial beam blockage can affect classification.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Cloud Classification of AVHRR Imagery in Maritime Regions Using a Probabilistic Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1994)033<0909:ccoaii>2.0.co;2)
Bankert (1994), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 170 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates cloud classification of satellite imagery over maritime regions to support analysts and forecasters.
- **Architecture:** Probabilistic neural network classifier using spectral and textural features from image samples, with feature selection to reduce the feature set.
- **Data:** AVHRR imagery samples over maritime regions labelled by experts into about ten cloud classes.
- **Main result:** The probabilistic neural network achieves overall classification accuracy of roughly 80% on independent samples, with confusion mainly between similar cloud types.
- **Open work:** Extending to other regions and sensors and adding multi-layer or nighttime classes.
- **Issues:** Relies on subjective expert labels and fixed-size sample boxes that may contain mixed cloud types.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Hydrometeor classification system using dual-polarization radar measurements: model improvements and in situ verification](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2004.843077)
Lim et al. (2005), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 168 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves dual-polarization radar hydrometeor classification and verifies it with in situ observations.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic hydrometeor classification using polarimetric variables, with refined membership functions.
- **Data:** CSU-CHILL S-band polarimetric radar observations with in situ hydrometeor observations for verification.
- **Main result:** The improved classifier matches in situ hydrometeor observations well.
- **Open work:** Applying to other radars and climates.
- **Issues:** Limited verification cases; membership functions tuned to S-band.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Global wind speed retrieval from SAR](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2003.814658)
Horstmann et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 167 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves ocean surface wind speeds globally from synthetic aperture radar imagery.
- **Architecture:** Neural network inversion of a C-band geophysical model function using SAR backscatter and wind direction from image streaks.
- **Data:** ERS-2 SAR imagery worldwide compared with ECMWF model winds.
- **Main result:** SAR wind retrievals agree well with model winds globally.
- **Open work:** Improved direction retrieval and use of Envisat ASAR.
- **Issues:** Dependent on model function; validation against model winds.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Development of a sky imager for cloud cover assessment.](https://doi.org/10.1364/josaa.25.000029)
Cazorla et al. (2008), *Journal of The Optical Society of America A-optics Image Science and Vision*. 167 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops an all-sky imager to assess cloud cover automatically.

- **Data:** Sky images from Granada, Spain.
- **Main result:** The imager estimates cloud cover in good agreement with observers.

- **Issues:** Sun glare and horizon effects.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Weather Radar Ground Clutter. Part II: Real-Time Identification and Filtering](https://doi.org/10.1175/2009jtecha1160.1)
Hubbert et al. (2009), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 166 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies ground clutter in weather radar data in real time so that clutter filtering is applied only where needed, avoiding bias in precipitation echoes from indiscriminate filtering.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic Clutter Mitigation Decision (CMD) algorithm combining clutter phase alignment and reflectivity texture/spin features, followed by a spectral clutter filter (GMAP) at flagged gates; not a trained ML model.
- **Data:** S-band research and operational Doppler radar time series (NCAR S-Pol and NEXRAD-type data); exact cases not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Selective clutter filtering guided by the fuzzy decision removes clutter while largely preserving weather echoes that overlap clutter regions.
- **Open work:** Extension to other radar wavelengths and scanning strategies and tuning of membership functions for different clutter environments.
- **Issues:** Hand-designed membership functions and thresholds; performance in mixed clutter-weather gates and anomalous propagation depends on site tuning.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Pattern Recognition Technique for Distinguishing Surface and Cloud Types in the Polar Regions](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1987)026<1412:aprtfd>2.0.co;2)
Ebert (1987), *Venue not recorded*. 156 citations.

- **Main goal:** Distinguishes clouds from snow and ice surfaces in polar satellite imagery, which is difficult with simple thresholds.

- **Data:** AVHRR imagery over polar regions with expert-labelled samples covering many surface and cloud classes.
- **Main result:** Combining spectral and textural features separates most surface and cloud types in polar scenes with good accuracy; specific figures not reported here.
- **Open work:** Application to climatological cloud analysis and extension to more seasons and sensors.
- **Issues:** Depends on expert labelling and limited training scenes; low sun angles and thin cloud remain problematic.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A two-parameter wind speed algorithm for Ku-band altimeters](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(2002)019<2030:atpwsa>2.0.co;2)
Gourrion et al. (2002), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 153 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves wind speed retrieval from Ku-band satellite altimeters by accounting for sea state, not only backscatter.
- **Architecture:** Two-parameter wind speed algorithm using backscatter coefficient and significant wave height, fitted with a small neural network.
- **Data:** Satellite altimeter data (TOPEX/Poseidon) collocated with scatterometer and buoy wind measurements.
- **Main result:** Including significant wave height reduces wind speed retrieval errors relative to single-parameter algorithms.
- **Open work:** Adapting the algorithm to other altimeters and bands.
- **Issues:** Calibration depends on collocated reference winds; sea-state effects beyond wave height not captured.

### [A Fuzzy Logic Technique for Identifying Nonprecipitating Echoes in Radar Scans](https://doi.org/10.1175/jtech1914.1)
Berenguer et al. (2006), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 152 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies nonprecipitating echoes (ground clutter, anomalous propagation) in weather radar scans to improve radar rainfall estimates.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy logic classification using reflectivity texture and vertical structure features from volume scans; not a trained ML model.
- **Data:** Single-polarization C-band radar volume scans in Catalonia, Spain.

### [Rainfall Estimation from a Combination of TRMM Precipitation Radar and GOES Multispectral Satellite Imagery through the Use of an Artificial Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(2001)040<2115:refaco>2.0.co;2)
Bellerby et al. (2000), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 149 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates rainfall at high temporal resolution by combining satellite precipitation radar with geostationary imagery.

- **Data:** TRMM Precipitation Radar overpasses collocated with GOES multispectral imagery.
- **Main result:** The neural network produces rainfall estimates that improve on simple infrared-based techniques when validated against radar rainfall.

- **Issues:** Training limited to PR overpass samples; IR-based relations are weaker for warm rain.

### [Polar Cloud and Surface Classification Using AVHRR Imagery: An Intercomparison of Methods](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1992)031<0405:pcascu>2.0.co;2)
Welch et al. (1992), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 147 citations.

- **Main goal:** Compares methods for classifying clouds and surface types in polar AVHRR imagery, where cloud and snow/ice are spectrally similar.
- **Architecture:** Intercomparison of classification methods, including statistical classifiers and a neural network, using spectral and textural features.
- **Data:** AVHRR imagery over polar regions with expert-labelled samples.
- **Main result:** Neural network and statistical classifiers achieve comparable and generally good accuracy; specific values not reported here.
- **Open work:** Combining methods and testing across seasons and regions.

### [A neural-network technique for the retrieval of atmospheric temperature and moisture profiles from high spectral resolution sounding data](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2005.855071)
Blackwell (2005), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 133 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves atmospheric temperature and moisture profiles quickly and accurately from hyperspectral infrared sounder radiances.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network applied to radiances compressed by projected principal components (PPC/NN).
- **Data:** Simulated and observed AIRS hyperspectral radiances with radiosonde and NWP-based profiles (e.g., NOAA88 sounding set).

### [AIRS/AMSU/HSB precipitation estimates](https://doi.org/10.1109/tgrs.2002.808322)
Chen et al. (2003), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 131 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates global precipitation rates from the Aqua satellite microwave and infrared sounders (AIRS, AMSU, HSB), extending sounder-based retrievals to precipitation.

- **Data:** AIRS/AMSU/HSB observations from the Aqua satellite; neural network trained and evaluated against NEXRAD radar precipitation estimates.

### [A Deep Neural Network Modeling Framework to Reduce Bias in Satellite Precipitation Products](https://doi.org/10.1175/jhm-d-15-0075.1)
Tao et al. (2016), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 130 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reduces systematic bias in satellite infrared-based precipitation estimates, which suffer from a weak link between cloud-top properties and surface rain.

### [Convective Boundary Layer Depth: Improved Measurement by Doppler Radar Wind Profiler Using Fuzzy Logic Methods](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0426(2002)019<1745:cbldim>2.0.co;2)
Bianco et al. (2002), *Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology*. 130 citations.
