### [SpecTf: Transformers enable data-driven imaging spectroscopy cloud detection](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2502903122)
Lee et al. (2025), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects clouds, including thin cirrus, in hyperspectral VSWIR imaging spectroscopy where clouds distort quantitative retrievals.
- **Architecture:** Spectroscopic Transformer (SpecTf), a transformer operating on per-pixel spectra with interpretable attention.
- **Data:** EMIT imaging spectrometer data with cloud labels; tested for transfer to other imaging spectrometers (details not in the abstract).
- **Main result:** Produces highly accurate, robust cloud masks, learns physically meaningful spectral features and generalizes between instruments.
- **Open work:** Develop instrument-agnostic models for new orbital imaging spectrometers.
- **Issues:** Quantitative accuracy and comparison baselines not given in the abstract; depends on quality of cloud labels.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Cloud Identification Using Genetic Algorithms and Massively Parallel Computation
Buckles et al. (1996), *Venue not recorded*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Identifies cloud types or cloud regions in satellite imagery efficiently using evolutionary search.
- **Architecture:** Genetic algorithm for cloud identification executed on massively parallel computing hardware.
- **Data:** Satellite imagery of clouds; sensor and dataset size are not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Demonstrates that genetic algorithms on parallel hardware can identify clouds in imagery with practical speed; accuracy figures not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Comparison with other classifiers and scaling to operational image volumes.
- **Issues:** Limited evaluation; genetic algorithm results depend on fitness design and parameter tuning.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Neural network system for cloud classification from satellite images](https://doi.org/10.1109/ijcnn.1999.830756)
Torsum et al. (1999), *IJCNN'99. International Joint Conference on Neural Networks. Proceedings (Cat. No.99CH36339)*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates classification of cloud types from satellite images.
- **Architecture:** Neural network classification system for cloud types; detailed architecture not reported in the available record.
- **Data:** Satellite images with labelled cloud classes; sensor and sample sizes not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Reports that the neural network system classifies clouds with useful accuracy; numbers not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Wider validation over seasons and regions and comparison with other classifiers.
- **Issues:** Depends on expert-labelled training samples; generalisation beyond the studied scenes is uncertain.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Evolving expert neural networks for meteorological rainfall estimations](https://doi.org/10.1109/iconip.1999.845660)
McCullagh et al. (1999), *ICONIP'99. ANZIIS'99 & ANNES'99 & ACNN'99. 6th International Conference on Neural Information Processing. Proceedings (Cat. No.99EX378)*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves rainfall estimation from meteorological data, which single backpropagation networks handle poorly because of interference between sub-tasks.
- **Architecture:** Modular system of expert multilayer perceptrons (backpropagation neural networks), each specialising in a rainfall band (low, medium, high), with combined outputs; networks are evolved.
- **Data:** Meteorological observations used for rainfall estimation; region and period are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Expert networks improve both individual band classifications and overall rainfall classification accuracy compared with a single network; numbers not given in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Better methods to combine expert outputs and testing on additional sites and rainfall regimes.
- **Issues:** Rainfall is treated as classification into bands rather than continuous amounts; no independent dataset details or uncertainty.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Bayesian retrieval of scatterometer wind fields
Cornford et al. (1999), *Venue not recorded*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Retrieves consistent ocean surface wind fields from scatterometer data while handling the directional ambiguities of local inversions.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian framework combining neural network local models of the scatterometer inverse problem (mixture density networks) with a Gaussian process prior on wind fields.
- **Data:** ERS scatterometer backscatter with collocated NWP model winds; exact period not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Shows that Bayesian field-wise retrieval produces plausible, ambiguity-resolved wind fields; quantitative comparisons not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Efficient sampling of multimodal posteriors and operational testing.
- **Issues:** Multimodal posteriors are hard to explore; training winds from NWP introduce model biases.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Analysis of cloud type and distribution using NOAA-AVHRR-APT data and ground observations in the Upper Rhine Valley](https://doi.org/10.1109/igarss.1993.322407)
Heinzmann (1993), *IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyses cloud types and their spatial distribution over the Upper Rhine Valley.
- **Architecture:** Classification of cloud types from satellite imagery combined with ground observations; method details not reported in the available record.
- **Data:** NOAA AVHRR APT satellite images and ground-based cloud observations in the Upper Rhine Valley.
- **Main result:** Describes cloud type distributions derived from AVHRR APT data and their agreement with ground observations; quantitative results not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Longer records and higher-resolution AVHRR HRPT data.
- **Issues:** APT data have low radiometric and spatial quality; regional study.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deep Learning for Multi-Satellite Precipitation Retrievals: Impact of Tomorrow.io’s Microwave Sounders](https://doi.org/10.1175/jhm-d-25-0007.1)
Cannon et al. (2026), *Journal of Hydrometeorology*. 3 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops satellite precipitation retrieval for regions lacking radar, evaluating the benefit of commercial Tomorrow.io microwave sounders.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network ingesting sequences of geostationary imagery and sparse polar-orbiting passive microwave swaths over the preceding hour.
- **Data:** Geostationary imagers, public passive microwave sensors and two Tomorrow.io microwave sounders; verified against radar networks (USA, Europe, Japan), US gauges, and IMERG-Early.
- **Main result:** 10-min, 0.04° precipitation over 60°S–72°N; 5–10% gains over earlier versions and 30–50% skill gains over IMERG-Early; data denial for 2024 hurricanes shows microwave benefit.
- **Open work:** Add more sounders and extend validation to data-poor regions.
- **Issues:** Depends on commercial satellite data; validation mostly over radar-rich regions.
- *Basis: abstract*

<a id="extremes"></a>
## Extremes & tropical cyclones

### A data mining approach to predict forest fires using meteorological data
Cortez et al. (2007), *Venue not recorded*. 468 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts burned area of forest fires from meteorological data to support firefighting resource management.
- **Architecture:** Comparison of five data mining techniques including support vector machines (SVM), random forest, neural network, decision tree and multiple regression.
- **Data:** Real-world fire and weather data from the Montesinho natural park, northeast Portugal.
- **Main result:** SVM with temperature, relative humidity, rain and wind gives the best configuration, predicting small fires well.
- **Open work:** Better prediction of large, rare fires.
- **Issues:** Small dataset; large fires poorly predicted.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Application of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for Detecting Extreme Weather in Climate Datasets](https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.01156)
Liu et al. (2016), *arXiv*. 387 citations.

- **Main goal:** Replaces subjective threshold-based detection of extreme weather events in climate data with learned pattern recognition.
- **Architecture:** Deep convolutional neural network classifiers tuned with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, one per event type.
- **Data:** Labeled image patches from climate simulations and reanalysis (e.g., CAM5 output) for tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers and weather fronts.
- **Main result:** Classification accuracy of about 89% to 99% for tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers and weather fronts.
- **Open work:** Moving from patch classification to localization and segmentation in full global fields, and reducing reliance on labels.
- **Issues:** Labels come from heuristic detection schemes, so the CNN learns those definitions; classification of pre-cropped patches, not detection in raw data.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Exascale Deep Learning for Climate Analytics](https://doi.org/10.1109/sc.2018.00054)
Kurth et al. (2018), *International Conference for High Performance Computing, Networking, Storage and Analysis*. 286 citations.

- **Main goal:** Scales deep learning for pixel-level segmentation of extreme weather patterns in climate data to the largest supercomputers.
- **Architecture:** Segmentation networks (Tiramisu and DeepLabv3+ variants) with improved software frameworks, input pipeline and distributed training algorithms.
- **Data:** High-resolution CAM5 climate simulation output with heuristic labels for tropical cyclones and atmospheric rivers.
- **Main result:** DeepLabv3+ scales to 27,360 V100 GPUs at 325.8 PF/s sustained (90.7% efficiency); FP16 reaches 1.13 EF/s peak and 999 PF/s sustained; Gordon Bell Prize winner.
- **Open work:** Improving label quality and using segmentations for scientific analysis of extremes under climate change.
- **Issues:** Focus is computing performance; labels from heuristic detectors; scientific accuracy evaluation is limited.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Tornado Detection with Support Vector Machines](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-44864-0_30)
Trafalis et al. (2003), *International Conference on Conceptual Structures*. 278 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves tornado detection from Doppler radar to reduce false alarms and missed tornadoes.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machines, compared with neural networks and other classifiers.
- **Data:** Attributes from the WSR-88D mesocyclone detection algorithm for radar-observed circulations.
- **Main result:** Support vector machines outperform the neural network and the baseline in skill scores for discriminating tornadic from non-tornadic circulations.
- **Open work:** Larger datasets, feature selection and probabilistic outputs for operational warning.
- **Issues:** Rare-event class imbalance and limited sample size; offline evaluation only.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Tropical Cyclone Intensity Estimation Using a Deep Convolutional Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1109/tip.2017.2766358)
Pradhan et al. (2018), *IEEE Transactions on Image Processing*. 229 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimate tropical cyclone intensity directly from satellite imagery as an objective alternative to the subjective Dvorak technique.
- **Architecture:** Deep convolutional neural network regressing (or classifying) intensity from infrared satellite images of tropical cyclones.
- **Data:** Geostationary infrared hurricane images matched with best-track intensities (Atlantic and Pacific basins); exact period not available here.
- **Main result:** Reported RMSE of roughly 10 kt relative to best-track intensity, competitive with existing objective techniques; numbers should be checked against the paper.
- **Open work:** Adding temporal information, multiple channels and other basins; operational testing.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; best-track labels are themselves uncertain (partly Dvorak-based); relatively small sample of intense storms.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Neural Network for Tornado Prediction Based on Doppler Radar-Derived Attributes](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(1996)035<0617:annftp>2.0.co;2)
Marzban et al. (1996), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 212 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts which radar-detected circulations will be associated with tornadoes, to improve tornado warnings.
- **Architecture:** Multilayer perceptron neural network using Doppler radar-derived attributes, compared with rule-based, discriminant analysis and logistic regression methods.
- **Data:** Attributes from the NSSL mesocyclone detection algorithm applied to WSR-88D Doppler radar data, with tornado reports as ground truth.
- **Main result:** The neural network outperforms the rule-based algorithm and statistical methods on several skill scores.
- **Open work:** Larger datasets, additional attributes and probabilistic outputs.
- **Issues:** Limited number of tornado cases; results depend on the detection algorithm and attribute quality.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Analog Forecasting of Extreme‐Causing Weather Patterns Using Deep Learning](https://doi.org/10.1029/2019ms001958)
Chattopadhyay et al. (2019), *Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems*. 187 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predict extreme-causing circulation patterns days ahead with a fast data-driven analog approach to complement NWP early warnings.
- **Architecture:** Capsule neural networks with impact-based auto-labeling of Z500 patterns (classes 0-4 by occurrence and region of surface temperature extremes), compared with CNNs and logistic regression.
- **Data:** Large-ensemble fully coupled Earth system model output (CESM Large Ensemble) for North America.
- **Main result:** Using Z500 only, accuracies (recalls) of 69-45% (77-48%) for cold and 62-41% (73-47%) for heat waves at 1-5 days; with surface temperature added, about 80% (88%); CapsNets beat CNN and logistic regression and degrade least with less data.
- **Open work:** Testing on reanalysis and observations and combining with NWP for early warning.
- **Issues:** Trained and evaluated on model data only; coarse categorical targets; accuracy drops quickly with lead time.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Interpretable Deep Learning for Spatial Analysis of Severe Hailstorms](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-18-0316.1)
Gagne et al. (2019), *Monthly Weather Review*. 166 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predict severe hail probability from storm-scale model fields and interpret what the deep learning model learns.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network compared with logistic regression on spatial-mean or PCA inputs; interpretation via feature importance and feature optimization.
- **Data:** Storm-centered patches from NCAR convection-allowing ensemble runs, 3 May-3 June 2016; target is Thompson hail size diagnostic exceeding 25 mm in the next hour.
- **Main result:** CNN significantly outperforms all baselines in Brier skill score and ROC AUC; interpretation reveals physically consistent features (steep lapse rates, shear favoring wide updrafts) and storm modes.
- **Open work:** Verification against observed hail and longer, multi-season datasets.
- **Issues:** Target is a model diagnostic, not observed hail; one month of data; results tied to one model configuration.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A hybrid CNN-LSTM model for typhoon formation forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10707-019-00355-0)
Chen et al. (2019), *GeoInformatica*. 165 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts tropical cyclone (typhoon) formation, which is hard to anticipate with conventional approaches, by learning spatio-temporal precursor patterns.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid CNN-LSTM model: a convolutional neural network extracts spatial features and a long short-term memory network models their temporal evolution.
- **Data:** Not reported here; the abstract is unavailable and the gridded atmospheric and oceanic inputs are not specified.
- **Main result:** The title indicates the hybrid model is proposed for typhoon formation forecasting; quantitative skill is not available.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times, other ocean basins and comparison with dynamical genesis forecasts.
- **Issues:** Genesis events are rare, so class imbalance and few positive examples limit evaluation; details unknown without the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Predicting Hurricane Trajectories using a Recurrent Neural Network](https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v33i01.3301468)
Alemany et al. (2018), *AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence*. 165 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts hurricane trajectories at 6-hour intervals to reduce economic losses and save lives, given the nonlinearity of weather data.
- **Architecture:** Fully connected recurrent neural network (RNN) applied over a fine spatial grid to reduce truncation errors.
- **Data:** National Hurricane Center (NHC) best-track data: latitude, longitude, wind speed and pressure at 6-hour intervals.
- **Main result:** The RNN is reported as competitive with methods used by the NHC and predicts hurricane paths up to about 120 hours ahead.
- **Open work:** Adding environmental steering fields and satellite data, and quantifying track uncertainty.
- **Issues:** Uses only track and intensity history without atmospheric fields; competitiveness with NHC is not quantified in the abstract; no probabilistic output.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Non-crossing nonlinear regression quantiles by monotone composite quantile regression neural network, with application to rainfall extremes](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00477-018-1573-6)
Cannon (2018), *Stochastic environmental research and risk assessment (Print)*. 164 citations.

- **Main goal:** Prevents quantile crossing and overfitting in nonlinear quantile regression, which produce nonphysical results such as a 10-year rainstorm exceeding a 20-year storm.
- **Architecture:** Monotone composite quantile regression neural network (MCQRNN), an MLP estimating multiple non-crossing quantiles with optional monotonicity, non-negativity and additive constraints.
- **Data:** Monte Carlo synthetic data from multiple functions and error distributions; annual maximum rainfall intensities at Canadian stations for Intensity–Duration–Frequency curves.
- **Main result:** MCQRNN outperforms benchmark models, especially for non-normal errors, and gives more robust and realistic IDF curve estimates than standard QRNN.
- **Open work:** Applying the constrained framework to other environmental extremes and to spatial or nonstationary IDF estimation.
- **Issues:** Small to moderate samples of annual maxima limit extreme-quantile reliability; station-based application without spatial pooling.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction of a typhoon track using a generative adversarial network and satellite images](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-019-42339-y)
Rüttgers et al. (2019), *Scientific Reports*. 163 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts typhoon tracks directly from satellite imagery, aiming to anticipate the future typhoon centre and cloud structure.
- **Architecture:** Generative adversarial network (GAN) that generates a 6-hour-ahead typhoon image from time series of satellite images, optionally with velocity fields.
- **Data:** Time series of satellite images of past typhoons affecting the Korean Peninsula; tested on 10 typhoons not used in training.
- **Main result:** Mean centre error of 95.6 km at 6 hours for 10 test typhoons; adding velocity fields significantly improves prediction.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times, better handling of sudden track changes and inclusion of more atmospheric fields.
- **Issues:** Only 6-hour lead time; sudden westward or northward turns are hard to predict; small test set; error larger than operational short-range track errors.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Storm-Based Probabilistic Hail Forecasting with Machine Learning Applied to Convection-Allowing Ensembles](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf-d-17-0010.1)
Gagne et al. (2017), *Weather and Forecasting*. 162 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces storm-based probabilistic hail size forecasts from convection-allowing ensembles, improving on simple proxies and physically based hail models.
- **Architecture:** Machine learning on identified storm objects, including random forest and gradient boosting regression trees that predict hail occurrence and size distribution parameters.
- **Data:** Storm objects from convection-allowing ensemble forecasts (CAPS Storm-Scale Ensemble Forecasts) verified against radar-derived Maximum Expected Size of Hail (MESH).
- **Main result:** Machine learning hail forecasts are more skilful than the physics-based HAILCAST and updraft-helicity baselines; exact scores are not reproduced here.
- **Open work:** Operational testing, calibration across seasons and model configurations, and better hail observations.
- **Issues:** Radar-estimated hail size is an uncertain verification target; trained on specific ensemble configurations; limited seasons.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Using Deep Learning to Estimate Tropical Cyclone Intensity from Satellite Passive Microwave Imagery](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-18-0391.1)
Wimmers et al. (2019), *Monthly Weather Review*. 157 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimate tropical cyclone intensity objectively from satellite passive microwave imagery, which sees inner-core structure under clouds.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network (DeepMicroNet) with probabilistic output, able to work from partial scans and tolerant of imprecise storm-center fixes.
- **Data:** Passive microwave images at 37 GHz and 85-92 GHz from multiple sensors, trained against global best-track intensities; evaluated on two independent years and against aircraft reconnaissance-aided best track.
- **Main result:** RMSE of 14.3 kt against all independent best track, 10.6 kt against reconnaissance-aided best track, and 9.6 kt using only higher-resolution TMI and AMSR-E; the 85-92 GHz band contributes most.
- **Open work:** Expand training data, use more advanced architectures, and better characterize performance for the strongest storms.
- **Issues:** Too few category-5 cases for conclusive results at high intensities; the model reproduces known best-track biases because it is trained on best track; microwave overpasses are infrequent.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [ClimateNet: an expert-labeled open dataset and deep learning architecture for enabling high-precision analyses of extreme weather](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-2020-72)
Prabhat et al. (2020), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 133 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides labeled data and a deep learning method for precise detection of tropical cyclones (TCs) and atmospheric rivers (ARs), since heuristic detection algorithms disagree strongly.
- **Architecture:** ClimateNet: community-sourced, expert-labeled segmentation dataset plus a semantic segmentation CNN (DeepLabv3+-style) for pixel-level TC/AR/background classification.
- **Data:** High-resolution CAM5.1 climate model output for a recent historical period (labeled), applied to historical and climate-change scenario CAM5.1 simulations.
- **Main result:** The trained model accurately segments TCs and ARs and enables event-conditioned statistics, e.g. regional distributions of extreme precipitation attributed to TCs or ARs.
- **Open work:** Extending to more event types and to observations and reanalysis via transfer learning; growing the labeled dataset.
- **Issues:** Labels are subjective and limited in number; trained on a single model's simulations, so transfer to other models or reanalysis is untested here.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A Neural Network Short-Term Forecast of Significant Thunderstorms](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0434(1992)007<0525:annstf>2.0.co;2)
McCann (1992), *Weather and Forecasting*. 131 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides short-term forecasts of significant thunderstorm occurrence to support forecasters.
- **Architecture:** Two multilayer perceptron (backpropagation neural network) models whose outputs are combined into a thunderstorm forecast product.
- **Data:** Hourly surface observation analyses of lifted index and moisture convergence over the United States, verified against thunderstorm reports.
- **Main result:** The neural network product gives useful 3-7 h thunderstorm forecasts and outperforms the individual input fields alone.
- **Open work:** Adding further predictors such as upper-air and radar data.
- **Issues:** Depends on surface data analyses only and was verified over a limited period.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Using machine learning to predict extreme events in complex systems](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1917285117)
Qi et al. (2019), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America*. 130 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts extreme events and anomalous statistics in turbulent dynamical systems, a grand challenge in complex natural systems.
- **Architecture:** Densely connected mixed-scale deep convolutional neural network (CNN) trained with a relative entropy loss and empirical partition functions.
- **Data:** Simulations of a truncated Korteweg–de Vries (tKdV) model, with training only from the near-Gaussian regime.
- **Main result:** The network shows uniformly high skill across statistical regimes, including highly skewed extreme events not seen in training.
- **Open work:** Applying the approach to other complicated high-dimensional systems.
- **Issues:** Idealized 1D test model; no real-world data; generalization to other systems untested.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A nowcasting model for the prediction of typhoon tracks based on a long short term memory neural network](https://doi.org/10.1007/s13131-018-1219-z)
Gao et al. (2018), *Acta Oceanologica Sinica*. 122 citations.

- **Main goal:** Nowcasts typhoon tracks with a deep learning model.
- **Architecture:** LSTM neural network, as stated in the title.
- **Data:** Not reported (no abstract); presumably historical typhoon best-track records.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Not reported.
- **Issues:** No abstract; data source, lead times and track errors could not be verified.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Estimating Tropical Cyclone Intensity by Satellite Imagery Utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf-d-18-0136.1)
Chen et al. (2019), *Weather and forecasting*. 116 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides an objective, consistent estimate of tropical cyclone intensity from satellite imagery to replace the subjective Dvorak technique.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network (CNN) adapted for regression, with an upgraded version adding TC metadata and post-smoothing.
- **Data:** Satellite infrared brightness temperature and microwave rain-rate images of 1097 global TCs, 2003–2014 training, 188 TCs (2015–2016) optimization, 94 TCs in 2017 for testing; best-track labels.
- **Main result:** RMS intensity difference of 8.39 kt against best track; 8.79 kt for a subset of 482 samples with reconnaissance observations.
- **Open work:** Adding more satellite channels and temporal information, and operational deployment.
- **Issues:** Best-track labels carry their own uncertainty; extreme intensities are rare in training.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Prediction of extreme precipitation using a neural network: application to summer flood occurence in Moravia](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0965-9978(99)00063-0)
Bodri et al. (2000), *Advances in Engineering Software*. 113 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts extreme precipitation linked to summer floods in Moravia, Czech Republic.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network; the specific architecture details are not specified here.
- **Data:** Precipitation records from Moravian stations, including the 1997 flood period.
- **Main result:** The neural network gives reasonable predictions of extreme precipitation. Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Including atmospheric predictors and longer records.
- **Issues:** Few extreme events; limited validation.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A Bayesian Neural Network for Severe-Hail Size Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0434(2001)016<0600:abnnfs>2.0.co;2)
Marzban et al. (2001), *Weather and Forecasting*. 113 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts severe hail size from radar and environmental data to improve warnings.
- **Architecture:** Bayesian neural network (MLP with Bayesian regularisation) for hail size classification.
- **Data:** WSR-88D radar-derived attributes and near-storm environmental sounding data with hail reports.
- **Main result:** The Bayesian neural network outperforms the existing hail detection algorithm in predicting hail size classes.
- **Open work:** Larger datasets and probabilistic calibration.
- **Issues:** Hail reports are biased; limited sample size.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Tropical Cyclone Track Forecasting Using Fused Deep Learning From Aligned Reanalysis Data](https://doi.org/10.3389/fdata.2020.00001)
Giffard-Roisin et al. (2019), *Frontiers in Big Data*. 112 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves fast 24 h tropical cyclone track forecasts with deep learning as a complement to dynamical and statistical models.
- **Architecture:** Fused neural network combining past trajectory data with reanalysis wind and pressure 3D fields in a storm-centered moving frame, predicting latitude/longitude displacement.
- **Data:** Over 3,000 storms from both hemispheres since 1979 at 6 h frequency, with aligned reanalysis fields.
- **Main result:** The fused network outperforms single-input variants and is competitive/complementary with current forecast models, producing forecasts in seconds.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times, intensity forecasting, and use of operational analyses/forecast fields as inputs.
- **Issues:** Only 24 h lead time; reanalysis inputs are not available in real time; specific error numbers not reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Money Doesn't Grow on Trees, but Forecasts Do: Forecasting Extreme Precipitation with Random Forests](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-17-0250.1)
Herman et al. (2018), *Monthly Weather Review*. 111 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produces probabilistic forecasts of locally extreme precipitation, which raw ensemble forecasts handle poorly.
- **Architecture:** Random forests trained on ensemble forecast predictors, per region, giving probabilities of exceeding return-period thresholds.
- **Data:** GEFS reforecast data as predictors, with observed extreme precipitation (relative to return-period thresholds) over the contiguous US as targets.
- **Main result:** Random forest forecasts are skillful and reliable, outperforming raw ensemble guidance and competitive with or better than operational human forecasts at short leads.
- **Open work:** Using convection-allowing model inputs and extending to longer leads and sub-daily accumulations.
- **Issues:** Rare-event sample size limits training; regional dependence; tied to one ensemble system. Abstract unavailable.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [A hybrid neural network model for typhoon-rainfall forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2009.06.047)
Lin et al. (2009), *Journal of Hydrology*. 109 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts rainfall during typhoons, which causes floods and landslides in Taiwan, with lead times useful for warnings.
- **Architecture:** Hybrid neural network model combining more than one network component; the component types are not specified here.
- **Data:** Typhoon events with rainfall gauge observations and typhoon characteristics in Taiwan; periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** The hybrid model forecasts typhoon rainfall more accurately than conventional neural network benchmarks; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and more typhoon events for training.
- **Issues:** Limited number of typhoon events; skill for unusual tracks is untested.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deep-Hurricane-Tracker: Tracking and Forecasting Extreme Climate Events](https://doi.org/10.1109/wacv.2019.00192)
Kim et al. (2019), *IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision*. 105 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tracks and forecasts hurricane trajectories in large-scale spatio-temporal climate data.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional LSTM (ConvLSTM) models applied to density maps of trajectories.
- **Data:** Twenty years of tropical cyclone records as pixel-level spatio-temporal histories; product not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** The ConvLSTM tracking model significantly outperforms existing approaches, and forecasts map well to ground truth.
- **Open work:** Extension to other extreme events and longer forecasts.
- **Issues:** Quantitative metrics are not reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Effective forecasting of hourly typhoon rainfall using support vector machines](https://doi.org/10.1029/2009wr007911)
Lin et al. (2009), *Water Resources Research*. 102 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts hourly typhoon rainfall for flood warning in Taiwan.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine (support vector regression) model, compared with multilayer perceptron neural networks.
- **Data:** Hourly rainfall and typhoon characteristics for typhoon events affecting a Taiwanese watershed; periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** The SVM-based model forecasts hourly typhoon rainfall more accurately and robustly than the MLP benchmarks; numbers not reported here.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and incorporation of radar data.
- **Issues:** Limited typhoon sample; accuracy declines with lead time.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deep Learning for Spatially Explicit Prediction of Synoptic-Scale Fronts](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf-d-18-0183.1)
Lagerquist et al. (2019), *Weather and Forecasting*. 98 citations.

- **Main goal:** Objectively identify synoptic-scale warm and cold fronts in gridded data.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network producing front probability grids followed by a novel postprocessing that converts probabilities to front objects.
- **Data:** 1000-mb wind, temperature, humidity, wet-bulb potential temperature and geopotential height from the North American Regional Reanalysis; labels from WPC human-drawn fronts.
- **Main result:** At a 250-km matching distance, POD 0.73, success ratio 0.65 and CSI 0.52, far exceeding a traditional numerical frontal analysis baseline.
- **Open work:** Front climatologies and quantifying frontal spread across NWP ensemble members.
- **Issues:** Human-analyzed labels are subjective and inconsistent; single pressure level; regional (North America) domain.

### [A Sparse Recurrent Neural Network for Trajectory Prediction of Atlantic Hurricanes](https://doi.org/10.1145/2908812.2908834)
Kordmahalleh et al. (2016), *Annual Conference on Genetic and Evolutionary Computation*. 98 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predict the trajectories of Atlantic hurricanes to support warning and preparedness.
- **Architecture:** Sparse recurrent neural network (RNN), with connectivity and training details not reported in the available metadata.
- **Data:** Historical Atlantic hurricane track data; the specific best-track product is not reported in the available metadata.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Inclusion of environmental steering predictors and comparison with operational track guidance.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; track-only inputs ignore the large-scale environment, and comparison with operational models is unclear.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Can AI weather models predict out-of-distribution gray swan tropical cyclones?](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2420914122)
Sun et al. (2024), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences*. 96 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether AI weather models can forecast extreme tropical cyclones stronger than anything in their training data (gray swans).
- **Architecture:** AI weather model (FourCastNet-type) retrained with Category 3-5 tropical cyclones removed from the training set.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis with strong cyclones removed for training; tested on Category 5 storms.
- **Main result:** The model cannot accurately forecast unseen Category 5 cyclones, but it can learn strong storms in one basin and forecast them in another.
- **Open work:** Methods to improve extrapolation to rare extremes, such as physics constraints or synthetic data.
- **Issues:** One model architecture; coarse reanalysis underestimates TC intensity anyway.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Avalanche forecasting — an expert system approach](https://doi.org/10.3189/s0022143000004172)
Schweizer et al. (1996), *Journal of Glaciology*. 95 citations.

- **Main goal:** Supports avalanche hazard forecasting by formalising expert knowledge.

- **Data:** Snow, weather and avalanche observations from the Swiss Alps.
- **Main result:** The expert system produces avalanche danger assessments in good agreement with observed avalanche activity and human forecasts; exact rates not reported here.
- **Open work:** Refining rules and combining with statistical methods.
- **Issues:** Rule base depends on expert input; verification is difficult due to sparse avalanche records.

### [Machine Learning for Real-Time Prediction of Damaging Straight-Line Convective Wind](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf-d-17-0038.1)
Lagerquist et al. (2017), *Weather and Forecasting*. 91 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predict in real time whether a convective storm will produce damaging straight-line wind, to support warning decisions.
- **Architecture:** Supervised machine learning on storm-object features, including tree ensembles such as random forests and gradient-boosted trees.
- **Data:** Radar-based storm tracks and radar statistics, near-storm environment soundings from a numerical model, and surface wind observations over the United States.
- **Main result:** Models skilfully predict damaging-wind probability at short lead times; detailed scores are not given here.
- **Open work:** Operational testing and use of convolutional networks on storm-centred radar images.
- **Issues:** Wind reports and observations are sparse and biased, so labels are noisy; damaging winds are rare events.

### [Tropical cyclone identification and tracking system using integrated neural oscillatory elastic graph matching and hybrid RBF network track mining techniques](https://doi.org/10.1109/72.846739)
Lee et al. (2000), *IEEE Trans. Neural Networks Learn. Syst.*. 87 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates identification and tracking of tropical cyclones in satellite imagery to support forecasting of their tracks.

- **Data:** Satellite cloud imagery of tropical cyclones; specific sensors and periods are not reported here (no abstract available).
- **Main result:** Not reported; no abstract is available for this paper.
- **Open work:** Evaluation on larger multi-season samples and comparison against operational track forecasts.
- **Issues:** Card based on the title only; accuracy figures and the size of the test set are unknown.

### [Cyclone track forecasting based on satellite images using artificial neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isprsjprs.2009.03.002)
Kovordányi et al. (2009), *Isprs Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing*. 83 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts tropical cyclone tracks directly from satellite images to complement numerical forecasts.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network applied to features extracted from satellite cyclone images; the specific network type is not specified in the available metadata.
- **Data:** Satellite images of tropical cyclones; sensors, basin and period are not reported here (no abstract available).
- **Main result:** Not reported; no abstract is available for this paper.
- **Open work:** Testing on larger cyclone samples and benchmarking against operational track forecasts.
- **Issues:** Card based on the title only; sample size and errors are unknown.

### [Deep Learning-Based Extreme Heatwave Forecast](https://doi.org/10.3389/fclim.2022.789641)
Jacques-Dumas et al. (2021), *Frontiers in Climate*. 77 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts the occurrence of rare, long-lasting extreme heatwaves using deep learning trained on climate model output.
- **Architecture:** CNN with large-class undersampling and transfer learning across intensity thresholds.
- **Data:** 1,000 years of climate model output (PlaSim) of surface temperature and 500 hPa geopotential height; heatwaves over France.
- **Main result:** The network forecasts long-lasting extreme heatwaves at three intensity levels up to 15 days before onset.
- **Open work:** Use as a proxy for rare-event resampling, climate change studies, and eventually real-world forecasting.
- **Issues:** Intermediate-complexity model; not tested on observations; class imbalance and limited number of extreme events.

### [Deep Learning on Three-Dimensional Multiscale Data for Next-Hour Tornado Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-19-0372.1)
Lagerquist et al. (2020), *Monthly Weather Review*. 75 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predict next-hour tornado occurrence for individual storms using deep learning on 3D radar and sounding data.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural networks on storm-centered 3D radar images plus Rapid Refresh proximity soundings, with hyperparameter experiments.
- **Data:** Multiradar composites MYRORSS and GridRad (separate models) with Rapid Refresh soundings; independent test data.
- **Main result:** AUC above 0.9 for both; CSI of 0.31 (GridRad, 3.52% event frequency) and 0.17 (MYRORSS, 0.24%); errors concentrate in nontornadic rotating supercells and tornadic QLCS cells.
- **Open work:** Implement in real-time forecasting and improve handling of QLCS tornadoes and rotating nontornadic supercells.
- **Issues:** Rare-event imbalance limits CSI; tornado reports used as labels have known reporting biases; performance varies strongly with dataset.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Physics-augmented Deep Learning to Improve Tropical Cyclone Intensity and Size Estimation from Satellite Imagery](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-20-0333.1)
Zhuo et al. (2021), *Monthly Weather Review*. 74 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves tropical cyclone intensity and wind-radii estimation from satellite infrared imagery by adding physical knowledge to deep learning.
- **Architecture:** DeepTCNet, a CNN augmented with auxiliary physical information (TC fullness) for single-task learning and with auxiliary tasks (intensity and wind radii) for multi-task learning.
- **Data:** Infrared satellite imagery of North Atlantic tropical cyclones with best-track intensity and wind-radii labels.
- **Main result:** Fullness augmentation improves intensity estimation by 12%, and multi-task learning improves wind radii by 6-9%. Intensity skill is 39% better than ADT on average and similar to SATCON; wind radii are 32% better than MTCSWA.
- **Open work:** Extend to other basins and add microwave imagery and other inputs.
- **Issues:** North Atlantic only. Labels come from best-track data with their own uncertainty, and fullness information may not be available in real time.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Forecasting Severe Weather with Random Forests](https://doi.org/10.1175/mwr-d-19-0344.1)
Hill et al. (2020), *Monthly Weather Review*. 72 citations.

- **Main goal:** Produce probabilistic Day 1-3 severe weather forecasts over CONUS analogous to SPC convective outlooks.
- **Architecture:** Random forests with separate models for tornado, hail and severe wind (Day 1) and regional models, using spatiotemporal fields such as CAPE, CIN and shear.
- **Data:** GEFS reforecast ensemble 2003-2012 for training; testing April 2012-December 2016 against storm reports and SPC outlooks.
- **Main result:** RF outlooks are calibrated, slightly underperform SPC at Day 1 but significantly outperform at Days 2 and 3; blends with SPC beat SPC alone at all lead days.
- **Open work:** Operational integration and use of higher-resolution or convection-allowing inputs.
- **Issues:** Coarse GEFS/R inputs; storm reports have population and reporting biases; feature importance is not physical causation.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Do data-driven models beat numerical models in forecasting weather extremes? A comparison of IFS HRES, Pangu-Weather, and GraphCast](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-17-7915-2024)
Olivetti et al. (2024), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 72 citations.

- **Main goal:** Testing claims that data-driven weather models are unreliable for extreme events by comparing them with ECMWF's physics model.
- **Architecture:** Evaluation study comparing Pangu-Weather (transformer) and GraphCast (graph neural network) with the physics-based IFS HRES in a semi-operational setting.
- **Data:** Global near-surface temperature and wind speed forecasts at 1-10 day leads, with IFS HRES as the reference model.
- **Main result:** Data-driven models mostly beat IFS HRES on global RMSE and compete on extremes in most regions, doing best for temperature extremes near the tropics at short leads.
- **Open work:** Overcoming remaining challenges before operational implementation.
- **Issues:** Performance varies by region, extreme type and lead time; deterministic models only.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Topological data analysis and machine learning for recognizing atmospheric river patterns in large climate datasets](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-12-613-2019)
Muszynski et al. (2019), *Geoscientific Model Development*. 71 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automatically recognize atmospheric rivers in large climate datasets without resolution-dependent detection thresholds.
- **Architecture:** Topological data analysis extracts shape features of integrated water vapor fields, which feed a supervised machine-learning classifier.
- **Data:** CAM5.1 climate model output and MERRA-2 reanalysis.
- **Main result:** Threshold-free method provides AR topology and statistics, applies across resolutions and scenarios without retuning, and is fast enough for large datasets.
- **Open work:** Applying the method to evaluate model AR biases and AR changes under different climate scenarios.
- **Issues:** Labels depend on an existing reference detection; classification of AR presence rather than full pixel-level segmentation; accuracy figures are not reported in the abstract.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Validating Deep-Learning Weather Forecast Models on Recent High-Impact Extreme Events](https://doi.org/10.1175/aies-d-24-0033.1)
Pasche et al. (2024), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 71 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether ML weather prediction models forecast rare, high-impact extremes and compound impacts as well as operational NWP, beyond standard benchmark scores.
- **Architecture:** Evaluation study comparing GraphCast (graph neural network), Pangu-Weather and FourCastNet (transformer/neural operator models) with ECMWF HRES through impact-centric case studies.
- **Data:** Case studies of the 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave, the 2023 South Asian humid heatwave and the 2021 North American winter storm; forecasts verified against reanalysis or analysis fields.
- **Main result:** ML models match HRES locally on the Pacific Northwest heatwave but underperform when aggregated over space and time, forecast the compound winter storm substantially better, and underestimate humid-heat danger over Bangladesh.
- **Open work:** Wider case-study-driven, impact-centric verification of ML models, and adding the variables needed for health-risk metrics such as humid heat.
- **Issues:** Only three events, so conclusions are not statistically general; ML models lack key variables (humidity-related heat indices), requiring substitute variables.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [FuXi-Extreme: Improving extreme rainfall and wind forecasts with diffusion model](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11430-023-1427-x)
Zhong et al. (2023), *Science China. Earth Sciences*. 71 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reducing the smoothing of ML weather forecasts at longer leads, which underestimates extreme weather intensity.
- **Architecture:** Denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) applied to refine the surface output of the FuXi model (a transformer-based ML weather model).
- **Data:** Five-day FuXi surface forecasts trained on ERA5 reanalysis, compared with ECMWF HRES; IBTrACS for tropical cyclone evaluation.
- **Main result:** FuXi-Extreme outperforms FuXi and HRES for extreme precipitation, 10 m wind and 2 m temperature; TC tracks better than HRES, but intensity worse.
- **Open work:** Improving tropical cyclone intensity forecasting and extending beyond 5 days.
- **Issues:** TC intensity still inferior to HRES; trained on reanalysis so inherits its biases.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A nearest-neighbor model for regional avalanche forecasting](https://doi.org/10.3189/172756401781819247)
Brabec et al. (2001), *Annals of Glaciology*. 67 citations.

- **Main goal:** Supports regional avalanche danger forecasting by retrieving historical days with similar conditions.
- **Architecture:** Nearest-neighbour model (analog method) using snow and weather variables with optimized variable weights.
- **Data:** Swiss snow, weather and avalanche observation records from the Swiss Federal Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research.
- **Main result:** The nearest-neighbour model forecasts regional avalanche danger with moderate skill and serves as a useful aid to forecasters.
- **Open work:** Better predictor selection and inclusion of snowpack stability data.
- **Issues:** Moderate accuracy; target danger levels are subjective; limited to Swiss regions.

### [A Neural Network for Damaging Wind Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0434(1998)013<0151:annfdw>2.0.co;2)
Marzban et al. (1998), *Weather and Forecasting*. 66 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts which radar-detected circulations will produce damaging winds, to improve severe weather warnings.

- **Data:** Attributes from the NSSL mesocyclone detection algorithm applied to WSR-88D Doppler radar data, verified against damaging wind reports.
- **Main result:** The neural network outperforms traditional statistical methods in discriminating damaging wind events; specific skill scores not reported here.

### [The Use of Sounding-Derived Indices for a Neural Network Short-Term Thunderstorm Forecast](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf898.1)
Manzato (2005), *Weather and Forecasting*. 65 citations.

- **Data:** Udine radiosonde soundings and lightning data in Friuli Venezia Giulia, Italy.
- **Main result:** The neural network improves thunderstorm forecast skill over single indices and linear discrimination.

### [Hurricane Forecasting: A Novel Multimodal Machine Learning Framework](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf-d-21-0091.1)
Boussioux et al. (2020), *Weather and Forecasting*. 64 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecast tropical cyclone track and intensity with ML by combining diverse data sources.
- **Architecture:** Hurricast: multimodal framework using deep encoder-decoder (CNN/GRU/transformer) feature extraction from spatial-temporal reanalysis fields, combined with statistical features in gradient-boosted trees.
- **Data:** Historical storm data (best track) and reanalysis fields; evaluation in North Atlantic and Eastern Pacific for 2016-2019 at 24 h lead.
- **Main result:** Comparable mean absolute error and skill to operational models at 24 h, computed in seconds; adding Hurricast to a consensus could improve over NHC official forecasts.

### [Regional Heatwave Prediction Using Graph Neural Network and Weather Station Data](https://doi.org/10.1029/2023gl103405)
Li et al. (2023), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 62 citations.

- **Main goal:** Gives timely, low-cost predictions of regional heatwave occurrence for preparedness.
- **Architecture:** Graph neural network over a network of weather stations, with an interpretable structure that reveals spatiotemporal links between locations.
- **Data:** Weather station observations; the region and period are not reported in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Reports high-accuracy real-time warnings of sudden regional heatwaves at low computational and data cost; no numbers in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Applying the framework to other extreme and compound climate events.

### [An Automated Method to Estimate Tropical Cyclone Intensity Using SSM/I Imagery](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0450(2002)041<0461:aamtet>2.0.co;2)
Bankert et al. (2002), *Journal of Applied Meteorology*. 62 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates estimation of tropical cyclone intensity from passive microwave imagery as an objective complement to the Dvorak technique.

- **Main result:** The method estimates maximum sustained winds with errors comparable to other objective techniques; exact RMSE not reported in the available metadata.

### [Modeling and simulating spatial extremes by combining extreme value theory with generative adversarial networks](https://doi.org/10.1017/eds.2022.4)
Boulaguiem et al. (2022), *Environmental Data Science*. 61 citations.

- **Main goal:** Models spatial dependence of climate extremes for risk assessment, overcoming limits of standard multivariate extreme value models and of plain GANs.
- **Architecture:** evtGAN, a generative adversarial network combined with extreme value theory for marginals.

### [Nearest neighbours for avalanche forecasting in Scotland—development, verification and optimisation of a model](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0165-232x(03)00075-2)
Purves et al. (2003), *Cold Regions Science and Technology*. 61 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops, verifies and optimises a nearest-neighbour model for avalanche forecasting in Scotland.

### MEPRA - An Expert System for Avalanche Risk Forecasting
Giraud (1992), *Venue not recorded*. 60 citations.

- **Main goal:** Supports operational avalanche risk forecasting by automating expert assessment of snowpack stability.
- **Architecture:** Expert system (rule-based) named MEPRA that applies avalanche-expert rules to simulated snow-cover stratigraphy to estimate instability and risk.
- **Data:** Snowpack profiles simulated by the CROCUS snow model driven by meteorological analyses in the French Alps (Météo-France).

### [Global Extreme Heat Forecasting Using Neural Weather Models](https://doi.org/10.1175/aies-d-22-0035.1)
Lopez‐Gomez et al. (2022), *Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems*. 59 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assess whether neural weather models can forecast extreme heat globally on short, medium and subseasonal timescales to support heat-wave warnings.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural weather models on the cubed sphere trained with candidate losses, including mean squared error and exponential losses that emphasize extremes, plus transfer learning.
- **Data:** ERA5 reanalysis, surface temperature anomalies at about 200 km resolution, 1-28 day lead times; compared with persistence and the ECMWF S2S control forecast.
- **Main result:** Extreme-focused losses significantly improve heat-wave skill with little loss in general skill; a symmetric exponential loss reduces smoothing; the best model beats persistence at all leads and the ECMWF S2S control after two weeks.

- **Issues:** Coarse resolution; comparison is against a single control forecast rather than the ensemble; regressive skill metrics only.

### [Objective Classification of Tornadic and Nontornadic Severe Weather Outbreaks](https://doi.org/10.1175/2009mwr2897.1)
Mercer et al. (2009), *Monthly Weather Review*. 59 citations.

- **Main goal:** Objectively distinguishes tornadic from nontornadic severe weather outbreaks from their large-scale environments, to improve outbreak-type forecasting days ahead.
- **Architecture:** Statistical classification of synoptic-scale meteorological fields for outbreak days; the specific classifier type is not specified here.
- **Data:** Historical United States severe weather outbreaks ranked by type, with gridded synoptic-scale meteorological fields; the exact dataset and period are not reported here.

- **Issues:** Limited sample of outbreaks, coarse synoptic fields that miss storm-scale processes, and dependence on how outbreaks are defined and ranked.

Manzato (2007), *Atmospheric Research*. 53 citations.

Fang et al. (2021), *Atmosphere*. 52 citations.

- **Main result:** Preliminary summary showing deep learning can extract image features of extreme weather and estimate occurrence likelihood.

### [Tropical and Extratropical Cyclone Detection Using Deep Learning](https://doi.org/10.1175/jamc-d-20-0117.1)

### [Predicting cyclone tracks in the north Indian Ocean: An artificial neural network approach](https://doi.org/10.1029/2006gl028353)
Ali et al. (2007), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 51 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts tropical cyclone tracks in the north Indian Ocean to improve warning for coastal populations.

### [Probabilistic forecasts of extreme heatwaves using convolutional neural networks in a regime of lack of data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00971)

Guastavino et al. (2021), *Scientific Reports*. 49 citations.

### [A Feed Forward Neural Network Based on Model Output Statistics for Short-Term Hurricane Intensity Prediction](https://doi.org/10.1175/waf-d-18-0173.1)

- **Main goal:** Improve short-term tropical cyclone intensity forecasts, including rapid intensification, by postprocessing HWRF output.
- **Architecture:** Feed-forward neural network using the operational current intensity estimate and HWRF-derived predictors, constrained to 6-h-old model data.
- **Data:** 2014-2016 HWRF reforecasts for Atlantic and eastern Pacific storms for training and cross-validation; real-time 2017 data for out-of-sample testing; best track for verification.
- **Main result:** Cross-validation shows lower MAE than HWFI at 3-57 h, but in 2017 HWFI was better at leads up to 24 h and similar later; the FFNN produced 4 times as many RI hits and higher Atlantic Brier skill than HWFI and SHIPS-RII.
- **Open work:** Retraining for newer HWRF versions, longer training sets and probabilistic intensity outputs.
- **Issues:** Short training period tied to a specific HWRF version; more RI false alarms; cross-validation gains did not fully hold in real-time testing.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Automatic tropical cyclone eye fix using genetic algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2006.10.013)
Wong et al. (2008), *Expert systems with applications*. 48 citations.

- **Main goal:** Automates fixing the tropical cyclone eye centre, a routine task otherwise done subjectively by forecasters.
- **Architecture:** Genetic algorithm optimization that fits an eye template to imagery to locate the cyclone centre; not a neural network method.
- **Data:** Weather radar imagery of tropical cyclones near Hong Kong.
- **Main result:** The genetic algorithm locates eye centres with accuracy comparable to manual best-track fixes for the tested cases.
- **Open work:** Extending to satellite imagery, weak or poorly defined eyes, and operational real-time use.
- **Issues:** Performance degrades for cyclones without a clear eye; evaluation covers a limited number of cyclones.
- *Basis: assessment*

Mudigonda et al. (2017), *Venue not recorded*. 47 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects, segments and tracks extreme climate events such as tropical cyclones and atmospheric rivers in large climate datasets to support automated analysis of extremes.

### [A Decision Tree Method of Forecasting Thunderstorms, Severe Thunderstorms and Tornadoes](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0434(1987)002<0337:adtmof>2.0.co;2)

### [Objective Prediction of Severe Thunderstorm Environments: Preliminary Results Linking a Decision Tree with an Operational Regional NWP Model](https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0434(1998)013<1078:oposte>2.0.co;2)

### [A deep learning ensemble approach for predicting tropical cyclone rapid intensification](https://doi.org/10.1002/asl.1151)
Chen et al. (2023), *Atmospheric Science Letters*. 44 citations.

### [Predictability Limit of the 2021 Pacific Northwest Heatwave From Deep‐Learning Sensitivity Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1029/2024gl110651)
Vonich et al. (2024), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 42 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates the predictability limit of the June 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave using gradient-based initial condition optimization in deep learning weather models.

Carr et al. (1994), *Venue not recorded*. 40 citations.

Carr et al. (2001), *Venue not recorded*. 37 citations.

### [Benchmark dataset and deep learning method for global tropical cyclone forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61087-4)
Huang et al. (2025), *Nature Communications*. 35 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves deep learning tropical cyclone track and intensity forecasts by providing an open multimodal dataset and a meteorology-informed model.

Watson (2022), *Environmental Research Letters*. 33 citations.

Zhang et al. (2025), *arXiv*. 27 citations.

Wang et al. (2025), *Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America*. 27 citations.

### [AI-Boosted Rare Event Sampling to Characterize Extreme Weather.](https://doi.org/10.1103/b1gc-9c2q)
Lancelin et al. (2025), *Physical Review Letters*. 18 citations.

Racah et al. (2016), *arXiv*. 17 citations.

DeMaria et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 16 citations.

Ho et al. (2008), *IEEE Aerospace Conference*. 16 citations.

Shi et al. (2025), *Journal of Geophysical Research*. 15 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses whether AI weather prediction models are reliable for severe weather by comparing operational tropical cyclone forecasts from Pangu-Weather with physics-based NWP.
- **Architecture:** Evaluation study of Pangu-Weather, a 3D Earth-specific transformer, run from different initial conditions and compared with ECMWF and NCEP numerical weather prediction models; no new model is trained.
- **Data:** Western Pacific tropical cyclones of 2023 in an operational context, with Pangu-Weather initialized from ECMWF and NCEP analyses and verified against best-track and analysis fields.

### [Predicting Beyond Training Data via Extrapolation versus Translocation: AI Weather Models and Dubai's Unprecedented 2024 Rainfall](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10241)
Sun et al. (2025), *arXiv*. 15 citations.

- **Main goal:** Investigates whether and how AI weather models forecast gray swan extremes lying beyond their regional training data, using the unprecedented April 2024 Dubai rainfall.
- **Architecture:** Analysis of graph neural network and transformer AI weather models (GraphCast, AIFS, FuXi) with fine-tuning experiments and receptive field analyses to separate extrapolation from translocation.
- **Data:** Operational-style forecasts of the 2024 Dubai storm, whose rainfall was twice the regional training maximum; models trained on ERA5 reanalysis.

Hua et al. (2025), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 15 citations.

- **Issues:** Hail is rare and locally observed, so labelled data are limited; unsupervised classes need interpretation.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Hurricane tracking via backpropagation neural network](https://doi.org/10.1109/icnn.1995.487576)
Johnson et al. (1995), *International Conference on Neural Networks*. 13 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts hurricane tracks from past positions using a neural network as an alternative to statistical track forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Backpropagation neural network (multilayer perceptron).
- **Data:** Historical hurricane best-track positions; basin and period not reported.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the abstract.
- **Open work:** Adding environmental steering predictors and comparing with operational models follows naturally.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; likely small sample and persistence-based inputs only.
- *Basis: assessment*

### Operational Decision Tree Avalanche Forecasting
Rosenthal et al. (2002), *Venue not recorded*. 13 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides operational avalanche forecasting support by predicting avalanche activity from weather and snowpack variables.
- **Architecture:** Decision tree (classification tree) models.
- **Data:** Historical meteorological and snowpack observations with avalanche occurrence records at a ski area; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Decision trees are reported to give usable operational forecasts of avalanche days; skill figures are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Adding snowpack stratigraphy predictors and testing at other sites.
- **Issues:** Rare events and site-specific records limit generality; avalanche observations are incomplete.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Knowledge-Based System for Forecasting Snow Avalanches of Chowkibal-Tangdhar Axis (J&K)](https://doi.org/10.14429/dsj.49.3853)
Naresh et al. (1999), *Defence Science Journal*. 12 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops a rule-based expert system to forecast direct-action snow avalanches on the Chowkibal-Tangdhar axis in Jammu and Kashmir.
- **Architecture:** Expert system (rule-based) in CLIPS with 358 rules, including 173 decision rules, on 28 snow-meteorological variables.
- **Data:** 1154 samples of snow-meteorological and snow-profile data; test on 63 avalanche-day and 54 non-avalanche-day samples.
- **Main result:** Predicts avalanche days with 76% efficiency; 28.2% of the 117 test samples are misclassified.
- **Open work:** Extending to other avalanche types and sites and refining rules follow naturally.
- **Issues:** Single region, small test set and hand-crafted rules; considerable misclassification rate.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [An integrated decision method for prediction of tropical cyclone movement by using genetic algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1360/03yd0144)
Yang et al. (2005), *Science in China Series D: Earth Sciences*. 12 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts tropical cyclone movement by combining several forecast methods.
- **Architecture:** Integrated decision method that uses a genetic algorithm to optimize the combination of forecast methods.
- **Data:** Historical tropical cyclone track data in the western North Pacific; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** The integrated method is reported to reduce track forecast errors relative to individual methods; numbers are not reported here.
- **Open work:** Incorporating NWP guidance and longer lead times.
- **Issues:** Statistical combination limited by member methods and sample size.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Deep Learning Atmospheric Models Reliably Simulate Out‐of‐Sample Land Heat and Cold Wave Frequencies](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025gl117990)
Meng et al. (2025), *Geophysical Research Letters*. 11 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether deep learning GCMs reproduce extreme heat and cold wave frequencies outside their training period.
- **Architecture:** Evaluation of the hybrid NeuralGCM and the purely data-driven DLESyM deep learning models against the conventional HiRAM high-resolution model.
- **Data:** All models forced with observed SST and sea ice over 1900–2020, focusing on out-of-sample 1900–1960.
- **Main result:** Both DL models reproduce the frequency and spatial patterns of land heatwaves and coldwaves with skill comparable to HiRAM; all perform poorly over parts of North Asia and North America in 1940–1960.
- **Open work:** Improve temperature persistence in data-driven models and test generalization to future warming.
- **Issues:** DLESyM overestimates event frequencies due to excessive temperature autocorrelation; early-century observations are uncertain; out-of-sample period is cooler, not warmer.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Evaluating Global Machine Learning Models for Tropical Cyclone Dynamics and Thermodynamics](https://doi.org/10.1029/2025jh000594)
Sahu et al. (2025), *Journal of Geophysical Research*. 11 citations.

- **Main goal:** Comprehensively evaluates machine learning weather models for tropical cyclone track, intensity and physical structure before they replace NWP.
- **Architecture:** Evaluation of GraphCast (graph neural network), Pangu-Weather, Aurora and FourCastNet (transformer and neural operator models) against three NWP models and observations.
- **Data:** Tropical cyclones across all tropical ocean basins; verification against observations (best track) and NWP forecasts.
- **Main result:** All MLWP models have mean track errors below 200 km at 96 h but underestimate maximum winds; they capture vorticity advection, low-level convergence and warm cores with weaker magnitude; Aurora performs best.
- **Open work:** Reduce intensity bias by addressing training data biases and the double penalty effect, e.g. through higher resolution or probabilistic training.
- **Issues:** Intensity low bias linked to reanalysis training data and double penalization; weaker structure magnitudes than observed.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [A fuzzy expert system to assist in the prediction of hazardous wind conditions within the Mediterranean basin](https://doi.org/10.1017/s1350482798001005)
Kuciauskas et al. (1998), *Meteorological Applications*. 11 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assists forecasters in predicting hazardous wind conditions in the Mediterranean basin, such as regional mistral and bora events.
- **Architecture:** Fuzzy expert system (fuzzy logic, rule-based) built from forecaster knowledge.
- **Data:** Numerical weather prediction output and observations for the Mediterranean; details not reported.
- **Main result:** Not reported in the record.
- **Open work:** Operational evaluation and extension to more wind regimes follow naturally.
- **Issues:** No abstract available; knowledge elicitation is laborious and rules are regime-specific.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Severe storm cell classification using support vector machines and radial basis function approaches](https://doi.org/10.1109/ccece.2001.933663)
Ramirez et al. (2001), *Canadian Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering 2001. Conference Proceedings (Cat. No.01TH8555)*. 11 citations.

- **Main goal:** Classifies severe storm cells from radar-derived features.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machines compared with radial basis function networks.
- **Data:** Radar-derived storm cell attributes; details not reported here.
- **Main result:** Support vector machines are reported to classify severe cells well relative to RBF networks; numbers are not reported here.
- **Open work:** More data and feature selection.
- **Issues:** Small, imbalanced datasets.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Constructing extreme heatwave storylines with differentiable climate models](https://doi.org/10.5194/wcd-7-393-2026)
Whittaker et al. (2025), *Weather and Climate Dynamics*. 10 citations.

- **Main goal:** Constructs plausible worst-case heatwave storylines to probe the upper bounds of extreme events for climate risk assessment at low cost.
- **Architecture:** Gradient-based optimization of initial conditions through the differentiable hybrid climate model NeuralGCM (dynamical core plus neural network physics).
- **Data:** Case study of the 2021 Pacific Northwest heatwave; compared with a 75-member ensemble. Initial-condition source not detailed in the abstract.
- **Main result:** Optimized trajectories produce heatwave intensity up to 3.7 °C above the most extreme of 75 ensemble members, with intensified blocking and amplified Rossby waves.
- **Open work:** Applying the method to other extremes and warmer climates, and quantifying the plausibility and likelihood of optimized storylines.
- **Issues:** Single event; physical plausibility depends on NeuralGCM fidelity at extremes; optimized initial conditions may be unrealistic and the likelihood of storylines is not quantified.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Applications of Classification Tree Methodology to Avalanche Data Management and Forecasting
Davis et al. (1992), *Venue not recorded*. 10 citations.

- **Main goal:** Applies classification tree methods to manage avalanche data and to forecast avalanche activity from weather and snowpack observations.
- **Architecture:** Classification tree methodology (CART-style decision tree).
- **Data:** Historical avalanche occurrence records with meteorological and snowpack observations from a ski area; site and period are not reported in the available information.
- **Main result:** Classification trees provide interpretable rules that discriminate avalanche from non-avalanche days; skill numbers are not reported in the available information.
- **Open work:** Testing on additional sites and seasons, and combining trees with other statistical forecasting methods, follow naturally.
- **Issues:** Avalanche events are rare and site-specific, so trees may overfit and transfer poorly across regions.
- *Basis: assessment*

### Condensed and Updated Version of the Systematic Approach Meteorological Knowledge Base Western North Pacific
Carr et al. (1997), *Venue not recorded*. 9 citations.

- **Main goal:** Condenses and updates the meteorological knowledge base of the Systematic Approach for tropical cyclone track forecasting in the western North Pacific, to support forecasters in judging numerical track guidance.
- **Architecture:** Knowledge base of conceptual synoptic patterns, environmental structures and transitional mechanisms for tropical cyclone motion, used in an expert-system-like forecaster aid; not a machine-learning model.
- **Data:** Western North Pacific tropical cyclone cases and numerical model track guidance used to define and refine the knowledge base.
- **Main result:** Provides a condensed, updated set of synoptic pattern and region conceptual models intended to be easier to apply in operational track forecasting.
- **Open work:** Testing the condensed knowledge base in operational forecasting and extending it to other basins.
- **Issues:** Relies on subjective forecaster pattern recognition; skill gains depend on consistent application; quantitative verification not reported in the available metadata.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### Analysis of Weather and Avalanche Records from Alta, Utah and Mammoth Mountain, California Using Classification Trees
Davis et al. (1996), *Venue not recorded*. 8 citations.

- **Main goal:** Analyzes weather and avalanche records to identify conditions associated with avalanche activity for forecasting.
- **Architecture:** Classification trees (decision tree) relating weather and snowpack variables to avalanche occurrence.
- **Data:** Long-term weather and avalanche records from Alta, Utah and Mammoth Mountain, California.
- **Main result:** Classification trees identify key weather variables and thresholds associated with avalanche days; accuracy figures not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Using the trees in operational avalanche forecasting and adding snowpack structure information.
- **Issues:** Avalanche records are incomplete and observer dependent; site-specific trees may not transfer; class imbalance of avalanche days.
- *Basis: assessment*

### [Systematic and Integrated Approach to Tropical Cyclone Track Forecasting. Part 2: Climatology, Reproducibility, and Refinement of Meteorological Knowledge Base.](https://doi.org/10.21236/ada301936)
Carr et al. (1995), *Venue not recorded*. 7 citations.

- **Main goal:** Refines the Systematic and Integrated Approach to tropical cyclone track forecasting by documenting climatology, reproducibility and an updated meteorological knowledge base.
- **Architecture:** Meteorological knowledge base of synoptic patterns, regions and transitional mechanisms used as an expert-system-like forecaster aid; not a machine-learning model.
- **Data:** Western North Pacific tropical cyclone cases and associated analyses used to build the climatology and test reproducibility.
- **Main result:** Shows the knowledge base pattern and region classifications can be applied reproducibly and provides their climatology.
- **Open work:** Linking the knowledge base to identification of numerical model track errors and operational testing.
- **Issues:** Relies on subjective classification by forecasters; focused on one basin; quantitative skill improvements not reported here.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Harnessing AI data-driven global weather models for climate attribution: An analysis of the 2017 Oroville Dam extreme atmospheric river](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11605)
Baño-Medina et al. (2024), *arXiv*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Explores AI weather models for fast storyline-based climate attribution, using the February 2017 Oroville Dam atmospheric river as a case.
- **Architecture:** Pretrained AI global weather models (GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, FourCastNet, SFNO) run with initial conditions perturbed by climate change signals; compared to a dynamical model.
- **Data:** Initial conditions perturbed with pre-industrial and late-21st-century temperature change signals; dynamical model simulations as pseudo-reality; AI ensembles over 500 members.
- **Main result:** AI models project a 5–6% increase in integrated water vapor over Oroville versus pre-industrial, consistent with the dynamical model, but generally weaker attribution signals, especially for late-21st-century.
- **Open work:** Use explainable AI to build confidence in physical responses and enable real-time attribution.
- **Issues:** Reduced extrapolation skill to out-of-distribution climates; models differ in geopotential-moisture-temperature dependencies; single event studied.
- *Basis: abstract*

### Avalanche Forecast: Experience Using Nearest Neighbors
Buser et al. (1984), *Venue not recorded*. 6 citations.

- **Main goal:** Supports regional avalanche danger forecasting by finding past days with weather and snow conditions similar to the current day.
- **Architecture:** K-nearest neighbour (nearest neighbours) analogue method that retrieves the most similar past days and reports their observed avalanche activity.
- **Data:** Historical daily weather, snowpack and avalanche occurrence records from Swiss Alpine observation stations; period not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Reports operational experience showing the nearest-neighbour method is a useful aid to avalanche forecasters; skill scores not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Better weighting of input variables and combination with snowpack stability information.
- **Issues:** Analogue method limited by the length and quality of the historical record; rare large avalanche situations have few neighbours.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Detection of bounded weak echo regions in meteorological radar images](https://doi.org/10.1109/icpr.1996.547297)
Lakshmanan et al. (1996), *Proceedings of 13th International Conference on Pattern Recognition*. 5 citations.

- **Main goal:** Detects bounded weak echo regions in weather radar images, a signature of strong updrafts in severe storms.
- **Architecture:** Image analysis and pattern recognition algorithm for detecting bounded weak echo regions in volumetric radar reflectivity; not described as a neural network.
- **Data:** Weather radar reflectivity volumes; radar network and dataset size not reported in the available record.
- **Main result:** Demonstrates automated detection of bounded weak echo regions in radar images; detection skill not reported in the available record.
- **Open work:** Validation over more storms and integration into severe weather warning algorithms.
