### [A Genetic Programming Approach to Rainfall-Runoff Modelling](https://doi.org/10.1023/a:1008132509589)
Savić et al. (1999), *Water Resources Management*. 222 citations.

- **Main goal:** Applies genetic programming to discover explicit rainfall-runoff model equations from data.
- **Architecture:** Genetic programming (evolutionary algorithm evolving symbolic expressions), compared with an artificial neural network and a conceptual model.
- **Data:** Rainfall and runoff records from the Kirkton catchment in Scotland.
- **Main result:** The evolved models perform comparably to or better than the conceptual model and the neural network, while yielding explicit equations.
- **Open work:** Testing on more catchments and incorporating physical constraints on evolved models.
- **Issues:** Single-catchment study; evolved expressions may be complex and lack physical interpretability.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A physical process and machine learning combined hydrological model for daily streamflow simulations of large watersheds with limited observation data](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2020.125206)
Yang et al. (2020), *Journal of Hydrology*. 221 citations.

- **Main goal:** Builds a fast, easy-to-use ML-based hydrological model for daily streamflow in large, data-limited watersheds while handling spatial variability and extreme flows.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural network (MLP) trained on synthetic data from the physically based distributed GBHM model and a stochastic rainfall generator, with a categorization approach for high flows and local-binary-pattern computer vision features for spatial rainfall patterns.
- **Data:** Synthetic case studies from GBHM simulations plus real data from the upper Chao Phraya Basin, Thailand.
- **Main result:** The combined GBHM-ANN-CA-CV model greatly improves accuracy in data-limited basins; computer-vision spatial features improve robustness and categorization greatly improves high-flow simulation.
- **Open work:** Apply to other basins and to changing-environment scenarios for water resource management.
- **Issues:** Relies on the physical model's synthetic data so inherits its biases; single real-world basin; hand-crafted CV features rather than learned spatial representations.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Continuous streamflow prediction in ungauged basins: long short-term memory neural networks clearly outperform traditional hydrological models](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-27-139-2023)
Arsenault et al. (2023), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 221 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether LSTM networks predict continuous streamflow in ungauged basins better than regionalized conceptual hydrological models.
- **Architecture:** Long short-term memory (LSTM) recurrent neural network trained regionally, compared with state-of-the-art hydrological-model-dependent regionalization methods (spatial proximity, physical similarity, etc.).
- **Data:** 148 catchments in northeast North America (Quebec region) with the same meteorological and geophysical descriptor data as the hydrological models; leave-one-out cross-validation.
- **Main result:** LSTM outperforms regionalized hydrological models in 93–97% of catchments and beats models calibrated on the target catchment in up to 78% of cases, robust to hyperparameter changes.
- **Open work:** Use LSTM-based regionalization as a new baseline and explore larger, more diverse regions.
- **Issues:** Regional study with relatively dense gauging; leave-one-out may overstate transfer to truly remote ungauged areas; no interpretation of internal states.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [River flow forecasting using artificial neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/s1464-1909(01)85005-x)
Dibike et al. (2001), *Physics and Chemistry of The Earth Part B-hydrology Oceans and Atmosphere*. 221 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts river flow with artificial neural networks and compares them with a conceptual rainfall-runoff model.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward neural networks: multilayer perceptron (MLP) and radial basis function (RBF) networks, compared with a conceptual rainfall-runoff model.
- **Data:** Daily rainfall and river flow from a catchment in the Apure River basin, Venezuela.
- **Main result:** Neural networks perform slightly better than the conceptual model for daily river flow forecasting.
- **Open work:** Combining data-driven and conceptual models and extending lead times.
- **Issues:** Single catchment; deterministic forecasts; abstract unavailable so details rely on recollection.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Runoff Forecasting Using RBF Networks with OLS Algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)1084-0699(1998)3:3(203))
Fernando et al. (1998), *Journal of Hydrologic Engineering*. 220 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts runoff using radial basis function networks with an efficient training algorithm.
- **Architecture:** Radial basis function (RBF) network trained with the orthogonal least squares algorithm, compared with a multilayer perceptron and statistical models.
- **Data:** Hourly rainfall and runoff data from a catchment in Japan.
- **Main result:** The RBF network forecasts runoff with accuracy comparable to or better than the alternatives, with faster training.
- **Open work:** Longer lead times and other catchments.
- **Issues:** Single-catchment study; limited testing on extreme events.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Benchmarking data-driven rainfall–runoff models in Great Britain: a comparison of long short-term memory (LSTM)-based models with four lumped conceptual models](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-25-5517-2021)
Lees et al. (2021), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 218 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether LSTM rainfall–runoff models work across Great Britain and how they compare with conceptual hydrological models.
- **Architecture:** LSTM and Entity-Aware LSTM (EA-LSTM) recurrent neural networks trained across many catchments, benchmarked against four lumped conceptual models.
- **Data:** Hydro-meteorological forcings and discharge for 669 catchments in Great Britain (CAMELS-GB).
- **Main result:** LSTM and EA-LSTM reach median NSE of 0.88 and 0.86, outperforming the conceptual models, with largest gains in north-east Scotland and south-east England.
- **Open work:** Add inputs describing groundwater, abstractions and percolation; use spatial performance patterns to refine conceptual models.
- **Issues:** South-east England remains hard to model because the LSTMs cannot learn groundwater processes and human abstractions from standard meteorological inputs.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Improved streamflow forecasting using self-organizing radial basis function artificial neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2004.03.027)
Moradkhani et al. (2004), *Journal of Hydrology*. 218 citations.

- **Main goal:** Explores one-step-ahead daily streamflow forecasting, a challenging task central to water resources system control.
- **Architecture:** Self-Organizing Radial Basis (SORB) function network: a Gaussian radial basis function architecture combined with a self-organizing feature map (SOM); compared with a multilayer feedforward network (MLP), SOLO and linear regression.
- **Data:** Daily streamflow from the semi-arid Salt River basin, Arizona; cross-validation compared with split-sample testing.
- **Main result:** SORB outperforms the MLP and SOLO networks for daily streamflow; linear regression is unreliable; cross-validation confirms the nonlinear input-output relationship.
- **Open work:** Extending to multi-step forecasts and other basins.
- **Issues:** Single basin; one-step-ahead only; deterministic forecasts.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [Flood forecasting using support vector machines](https://doi.org/10.2166/hydro.2007.027)
Han et al. (2007), *Journal of Hydroinformatics*. 216 citations.

- **Main goal:** Applies support vector machines to flood forecasting and examines their strengths and weaknesses compared with established methods.
- **Architecture:** Support vector machine regression (SVR) for flood flow forecasting, compared with benchmark models.
- **Data:** Rainfall and flow records from the Bird Creek catchment, USA.
- **Main result:** SVMs forecast floods well at short lead times but are sensitive to parameter selection and input choice, and performance degrades at longer lead times.
- **Open work:** Better parameter selection and handling of longer lead times.
- **Issues:** Single catchment; limited extreme events; abstract unavailable so details rely on recollection.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Hybrid forecasting: blending climate predictions with AI models](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-27-1865-2023)
Slater et al. (2023), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 215 citations.

- **Main goal:** Reviews hybrid hydroclimatic forecasting that blends dynamical weather/climate model predictions with statistical or AI methods to improve forecast skill.
- **Architecture:** Review of hybrid forecasting systems that use machine learning and statistical post-processing to integrate outputs of numerical weather prediction, climate, land, hydrology and Earth system models.
- **Data:** Review of literature covering subseasonal-to-decadal predictions of rainfall, temperature, streamflow, floods, droughts, tropical cyclones and atmospheric rivers.
- **Main result:** Hybrid systems can reduce dynamical model biases, avoid running costly land models, and combine sources of predictability across horizons, and are attracting growing attention.
- **Open work:** Physically explainable results, assimilating human influences, new ensemble techniques, seamless short-to-long lead prediction, land/ocean/ice initial conditions, spatial variability and operational uptake.
- **Issues:** As a review it offers no new quantitative benchmark; hybrid approaches depend on stationarity of learned relationships and on the quality of dynamical inputs.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [An ANN‐based model for spatiotemporal groundwater level forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1002/hyp.7129)
Nourani et al. (2008), *Hydrological Processes*. 215 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts groundwater levels in space and time in an aquifer where water level data are sparse.
- **Architecture:** Feedforward artificial neural network (MLP) for temporal forecasting at observation wells, combined with geostatistical interpolation (kriging) for spatial estimation.
- **Data:** Groundwater level, rainfall and related data from observation wells in a plain in Iran.
- **Main result:** The ANN-based model forecasts groundwater levels accurately and, combined with spatial interpolation, provides spatiotemporal maps.
- **Open work:** Including pumping and other hydrogeological inputs and testing in other aquifers.
- **Issues:** Single aquifer; spatial accuracy limited by well density; abstract unavailable so details rely on recollection.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Regional flood frequency analysis at ungauged sites using the adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2007.10.050)
Shu et al. (2008), *Journal of Hydrology*. 215 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates flood quantiles at ungauged sites through regional flood frequency analysis.

- **Data:** Flood quantiles and physiographic/climatic characteristics for gauging stations in Quebec, Canada.
- **Main result:** ANFIS estimates flood quantiles at ungauged sites more accurately than the compared ANN and regression methods.
- **Open work:** Extension to other regions and inclusion of uncertainty in quantile estimates.
- **Issues:** Regional dataset; quantile targets come from at-site fits; abstract unavailable.

### [Estimation and forecasting of daily suspended sediment data using wavelet–neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2008.06.013)
Partal et al. (2008), *Journal of Hydrology*. 212 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates and forecasts daily suspended sediment load using wavelet decomposition to improve neural network performance.
- **Architecture:** Wavelet-neural network: discrete wavelet transform decomposes flow series into subseries that feed a feedforward neural network (MLP), compared with a conventional ANN and sediment rating curve.
- **Data:** Daily river flow and suspended sediment records from US rivers; exact stations not reported here.
- **Main result:** The wavelet-neural network estimates sediment better than the conventional ANN and rating curve, especially for peak values.
- **Open work:** Systematic selection of wavelet type and decomposition level, and testing on more rivers and multi-step forecasts.
- **Issues:** Few stations; results depend on wavelet choice and decomposition level; no uncertainty estimates; abstract unavailable.

### [Artificial neural network approach to flood forecasting in the River Arno](https://doi.org/10.1623/hysj.48.3.381.45286)
Campolo et al. (2003), *Hydrological Sciences Journal*. 210 citations.

- **Main goal:** Forecasts flood water levels in the River Arno to support flood warning for the city of Florence, Italy.

- **Data:** Rainfall and water level data from the River Arno basin, Italy.
- **Main result:** The neural network forecasts water levels with good accuracy for short lead times.
- **Open work:** Extending lead times, adding rainfall forecasts and testing on other flood-prone basins.

### [Rainfall-runoff model usingan artificial neural network approach](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mcm.2004.10.012)
Riad et al. (2004), *Mathematical and computer modelling*. 210 citations.

- **Data:** Rainfall and runoff data from the Ourika basin, Morocco.
- **Main result:** The neural network simulates runoff better than regression approaches.
- **Open work:** Testing on more basins, at different time steps and against conceptual models.
- **Issues:** Single semi-arid mountain basin; limited data length; abstract unavailable.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Deep learning shows declining groundwater levels in Germany until 2100 due to climate change](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-28770-2)
Wunsch et al. (2021), *Nature Communications*. 208 citations.

- **Main goal:** Assesses how climate change will directly affect groundwater levels in Germany during the 21st century.
- **Architecture:** Convolutional neural network (1D CNN) groundwater level models driven only by meteorological inputs, applied to climate projections.
- **Data:** Groundwater level records at 118 sites across Germany; meteorological inputs (precipitation, temperature) from observations for training and regional climate projections under RCP2.6, 4.5 and 8.5.
- **Main result:** Significant declining trends at most sites under RCP8.5, strongest in northern and eastern Germany, with greater variability and longer low-level periods; much weaker effects under RCP2.6 and 4.5.
- **Open work:** Include anthropogenic factors such as extraction and land-use change, and extend to other regions.
- **Issues:** Excludes groundwater abstraction; extrapolation of data-driven models to future climates is uncertain; inherits climate-model biases.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [U-FLOOD – Topographic deep learning for predicting urban pluvial flood water depth](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2021.126898)
Löwe et al. (2021), *Journal of Hydrology*. 208 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides fast predictions of 2D maximum water depth maps for urban pluvial floods at locations and rain events not seen in training.
- **Architecture:** U-Net convolutional neural network (image segmentation architecture) taking hyetograph patterns and topographic inputs, with systematic input selection and hyperparameter tuning (97k to 260M parameters).
- **Data:** Hydrodynamic flood simulations for an urban area (Denmark) driven by natural rain events, with terrain and imperviousness rasters; evaluation on unseen locations and events.
- **Main result:** Five terrain-shape and imperviousness inputs are optimal; a 28M-parameter model works best; performance is similar to existing screening approaches with predictions in seconds.
- **Open work:** Balance temporal and spatial rainfall patterns in training data, improve spatial inputs, and couple U-FLOOD to dynamic sewer system models.
- **Issues:** Predicts only maximum depth, not flood dynamics; trained on simulated data so inherits simulator assumptions; sewer system effects not represented.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Downscaling recent streamflow conditions in British Columbia, Canada using ensemble neural network models](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-1694(01)00581-9)
Cannon et al. (2002), *Journal of Hydrology*. 207 citations.

- **Main goal:** Downscales recent streamflow conditions in British Columbia from large-scale atmospheric circulation.
- **Architecture:** Ensemble neural network models (multilayer perceptrons combined by averaging), compared with linear regression models.
- **Data:** NCEP/NCAR reanalysis atmospheric fields and streamflow records from watersheds in British Columbia, Canada.
- **Main result:** Ensemble neural networks reproduce streamflow conditions from circulation predictors better than linear regression models.
- **Open work:** Applying the downscaling models to GCM climate change scenarios and other regions.
- **Issues:** Predictors from reanalysis inherit its biases; stationarity of statistical relationships under climate change is untested; abstract unavailable.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Estimating Evapotranspiration Using Artificial Neural Network and Minimum Climatological Data](https://doi.org/10.1061/(asce)0733-9437(2007)133:2(83))
Zanetti et al. (2007), *Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering-asce*. 207 citations.

- **Main goal:** Estimates reference evapotranspiration when only minimal climatological data, such as air temperature, are available.

- **Main result:** The neural network estimates ET0 well using only air temperature data.

### [Advances in ungauged streamflow prediction using artificial neural networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhydrol.2010.02.037)
Besaw et al. (2010), *Journal of Hydrology*. 205 citations.

- **Main goal:** Predicts streamflow in ungauged basins, where no discharge records are available to calibrate models, using artificial neural networks.
- **Architecture:** Artificial neural networks; the specific network types are not given in the available metadata.

- **Main result:** Not reported in the available metadata.
- **Open work:** Transferability of trained networks to more diverse ungauged basins.
- **Issues:** Abstract unavailable; regionalization from limited gauged basins may not generalize across climates and physiography.

### [Experimental investigation of the predictive capabilities of data driven modeling techniques in hydrology - Part 1: Concepts and methodology](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-14-1931-2010)
Elshorbagy et al. (2009), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 205 citations.

- **Main goal:** Presents the concepts and methodology of a comprehensive experiment comparing data-driven modelling techniques in hydrology.

- **Data:** Five datasets from Canada and Europe: evapotranspiration, upper and lower layer soil moisture, and rainfall-runoff, each resampled into 12 groups of training, cross-validation and testing subsets.
- **Main result:** Defines a rigorous experimental protocol with resampled data groups that allows both prediction accuracy and uncertainty of each technique to be compared; results are deferred to Part 2.
- **Open work:** Implementing the experiment and analysing accuracy and uncertainty of each technique, reported in Part 2.
- **Issues:** No results in this part; conclusions limited to five datasets from Canada and Europe.
- *Basis: abstract*

### [GENETIC PROGRAMMING AND ITS APPLICATION IN REAL‐TIME RUNOFF FORECASTING 1](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-1688.2001.tb00980.x)
Khu et al. (2001), *JAWRA Journal of the American Water Resources Association*. 205 citations.

- **Main goal:** Develops genetic programming as a data-driven tool for real-time runoff forecasting, both as a stand-alone forecaster and as an error-updating scheme for a conceptual rainfall-runoff model.
- **Architecture:** Genetic programming (symbolic regression evolving forecast expressions), used directly and to update errors of the conceptual MIKE11-NAM model.
- **Data:** Rainfall and runoff records from the Orgeval catchment in France; exact periods not reported here.
- **Main result:** Genetic programming gives accurate short-lead runoff forecasts and, as an updating scheme, improves the conceptual model's real-time predictions.
- **Open work:** Test on more catchments and longer lead times, and compare with other updating schemes such as neural networks or Kalman filtering.
- **Issues:** Single small catchment; skill decays with lead time; evolved expressions can be hard to interpret physically.

### [Evolving neural network using real coded genetic algorithm for daily rainfall-runoff forecasting](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2008.05.024)
Sedki et al. (2009), *Expert systems with applications*. 205 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves daily rainfall-runoff forecasting by training a neural network with a real-coded genetic algorithm instead of gradient-based backpropagation.

- **Data:** Daily rainfall and runoff series from a semi-arid catchment in Morocco; exact record length not reported here.
- **Main result:** The genetic-algorithm-trained network forecasts daily runoff more accurately than the backpropagation-trained network, especially avoiding poor local minima.
- **Open work:** Extend to multi-step forecasting, other catchments, and hybrid evolutionary-gradient training.
- **Issues:** Single catchment; genetic training is computationally costly; no uncertainty quantification.

### [Evaluating Different Machine Learning Methods for Upscaling Evapotranspiration from Flux Towers to the Regional Scale](https://doi.org/10.1029/2018jd028447)
Xu et al. (2018), *Journal of Geophysical Research - Atmospheres*. 203 citations.

- **Main goal:** Upscales evapotranspiration from flux towers to the regional scale, where in situ measurements have limited coverage.

Konapala et al. (2020), *Environmental Research Letters*. 202 citations.

- **Main goal:** Combines process-based hydrologic models with machine learning to reduce structural errors while retaining physical consistency for streamflow simulation.

### [Deep learning convolutional neural network in rainfall–runoff modelling](https://doi.org/10.2166/hydro.2020.095)
Van et al. (2020), *Journal of Hydroinformatics*. 198 citations.

### [Global soil moisture data derived through machine learning trained with in-situ measurements](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-021-00964-1)
O et al. (2021), *Scientific Data*. 196 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides spatially continuous global soil moisture independent of satellite retrievals and land models by learning from in-situ measurements.

### [Modelling rainfall-runoff using genetic programming](https://doi.org/10.1016/s0895-7177(00)00274-0)
Whigham et al. (2001), *Mathematical and Computer Modelling*. 174 citations.

Hu et al. (2019), *Journal of Hydrology*. 173 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides rapid spatio-temporal flood inundation prediction with uncertainty, beyond point time-series forecasts.

- **Data:** Simulations from the Fluidity full model for the Okushiri tsunami test case.
- **Main result:** LSTM-ROM agrees well with the full model while reducing CPU cost by three orders of magnitude, enabling predictions in seconds.
- **Open work:** Real-time flood warning applications and more test cases.
- **Issues:** Single test case; trained on model output rather than observations; POD truncation may lose fine-scale features.

### [Forecasting Surface Water Level Fluctuations of Lake Van by Artificial Neural Networks](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11269-006-9022-6)
Altunkaynak (2007), *Water Resources Management*. 173 citations.

Anctil et al. (2004), *Environmental Modelling & Software*. 173 citations.

- **Issues:** Limited catchments; neural network sensitivity to training design.

Paloscia et al. (2008), *IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing*. 172 citations.

### [Combining binary decision tree and geostatistical methods to estimate snow distribution in a mountain watershed](https://doi.org/10.1029/1999wr900251)
Balk et al. (2000), *Water Resources Research*. 171 citations.

### [Training Machine Learning Surrogate Models From a High‐Fidelity Physics‐Based Model: Application for Real‐Time Street‐Scale Flood Prediction in an Urban Coastal Community](https://doi.org/10.1029/2019wr027038)
Zahura et al. (2020), *Water Resources Research*. 170 citations.

- **Main goal:** Provides real-time street-scale pluvial flood prediction for an urban coastal city, where physics-based 1-D pipe/2-D overland flow models are too slow for operational decision support.
- **Architecture:** Random forest surrogate model trained to emulate hourly water depths from a high-fidelity 1-D/2-D physics-based urban flood model, using topographic and environmental features.
- **Data:** Hourly water depths simulated by a high-resolution 1-D/2-D physics-based model at 16,914 road segments in Norfolk, Virginia, USA; two training scenarios (flood-prone streets only vs. all segments).
- **Main result:** The random forest achieves high predictive skill, best when trained only on the most flood-prone streets, and cuts run time by a factor of about 3,000 relative to the physics-based model.
- **Open work:** Testing on additional storms and cities, adding forecast rainfall and tide inputs for operational use, and quantifying surrogate uncertainty.

### [The suitability of differentiable, physics-informed machine learning hydrologic models for ungauged regions and climate change impact assessment](https://doi.org/10.5194/hess-27-2357-2023)
Feng et al. (2023), *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*. 170 citations.

- **Main goal:** Tests whether differentiable, physics-informed hydrologic models can extrapolate to ungauged regions and credibly predict decadal streamflow trends for climate change impact assessment.
- **Architecture:** Differentiable process-based hydrologic model (delta model) whose parameters are produced by a regionalized deep neural network (LSTM-based parameterization pipeline), compared against a pure LSTM.
- **Data:** CAMELS basins in the contiguous US with several meteorological forcings (e.g. Daymet, Maurer, NLDAS); random ungauged-basin (PUB) and regional holdout (PUR) cross-validation, plus decadal trend evaluation.
- **Main result:** Delta models approach or beat LSTM in PUB and clearly beat it in PUR on daily metrics and mean/high-flow trends, though low-flow trends are worse; untrained evapotranspiration keeps good seasonality and parameter fields stay spatially stable.
- **Open work:** Applying delta models to regional and global simulations, improving low-flow processes, and assimilating multi-source observations for climate impact studies.
- **Issues:** Low-flow trend skill lags LSTM; performance depends on forcing product; evaluated on US basins only, and trend credibility is judged on historical decades rather than true future climates.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [A deep learning-based hybrid model of global terrestrial evaporation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29543-7)
Koppa et al. (2021), *Nature Communications*. 170 citations.

- **Main goal:** Improves global estimates of terrestrial evaporation by learning transpiration stress, whose controls are complex and usually treated linearly.

- **Main result:** The hybrid model better estimates transpiration stress and evaporation globally against in situ data and satellite proxies.
- **Open work:** Extend the framework to Earth System Models.
- **Issues:** Limited sap flow and flux site coverage; training targets derived from measurement-based stress estimates.
- *Basis: abstract+knowledge*

### [Coupling machine learning methods with wavelet transforms and the bootstrap and boosting ensemble approaches for drought prediction](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2015.12.017)
Belayneh et al. (2016), *Atmospheric Research*. 169 citations.
